After a World Cup that delivered so much colour and drama, the final between Spain and Argentina will not last long in the memory.

Spain are World Cup winners for the second time after Ferran Torres’ goal in extra time secured a second star for La Roja, but Argentina offered nothing as Lionel Messi and the defending champions finally ran out of road.

Style of the teams

Spain love the ball and seek to control the game through meticulous passing (but some people also find this “boring”). Argentina like fouls and gamesmanship, breaking up the game and doing whatever it takes to win until one of their stars - and it is usually the greatest of all time in Lionel Messi - makes the difference (but some people also find this “dirty”).

Together, “boring” v “dirty”(to borrow a couple of phrases used elsewhere) is not a great combination. Add in that fact that both teams were playing their eighth match of an exhausting tournament, with Argentina looking particularly tired following several comebacks in the knockout stages.

So, it didn’t help the final that Argentina resorted to even more fouls, leading to Enzo Fernandez’s red card shortly before extra time. They failed to land a single shot before Ferran Torres fired Spain into the lead, having contributed very little to the spectacle until it was far too late.

open image in gallery Fernandez’s foul on Pau Cubarsi saw him sent off ( Getty )

All the delays

The final kicked off six minutes late, which wasn’t great, but it sounds pretty inconsequential when compared to the 27-minute delay between the end of the first half and the start of the second. Organisers Fifa had assured both teams before the final that the half-time show was expected to take around 20 minutes, but the delay to the World Cup final was actually much longer, which meant Fifa went even further in breaking their own rules. The game’s laws state half-time breaks should “not exceed 15 minutes”.

Appearing on the BBC, and speaking for maybe everyone, former England captain Wayne Rooney said the half-time show was “crap” - but Spain actually had one of their better periods of the game after half-time, creating several chances and dangerous moments. Spain then hit another delay, however, with the second hydration break. We may have got used to the three-minute stoppages throughout this World Cup, but they don’t help matches that desperately need some rhythm and flow.

A ‘ bobbly, dry’ pitch

Concerns were first raised about the state of the ‘New York New Jersey Stadium’ pitch weeks ago. Brazil star Vinicius Jr said following the 1-1 draw against Morocco that “because of the weather and the heat, the grass dries out quickly and the game ends up being very slow”. Sound familiar? On ITV, Ian Wright led criticism of the World Cup final pitch following the goalless first half between Spain and Argentina, calling the playing surface “ridiculous, poor, terrible” as well as “bobbly and dry” - hardly ideal conditions for slick attacking play and silky dribbling.

The weather

The 3pm ET kick-off time in New Jersey (8pm BST) was undoubtedly scheduled with the European TV market in mind as well as the local and South American audience. But starting in the middle of the afternoon and the hottest part of the day (27C / 80.6F) would not have helped the players, either. The New York New Jersey Stadium is a giant outdoor bowl exposed to the elements, unlike the semi-final venues in Atlanta’s Mercedes Benz Stadium and the Dallas Stadium in Texas which feature giant retractable roofs and benefit from air conditioning.

open image in gallery Messi and Argentina looked exhausted in the World Cup final ( PA )

… finals usually are like this!

Sure, this was not the 2022 World Cup final between Argentina and France. But the reason that match should be remembered as the greatest football match of all time is because it took place within what is usually the suffocating constraints of the biggest sporting event on the planet. When the stakes and pressure are so high and the margins between immortality and defeat are so fine, it does not tend to result in a thriller. England’s 6-4 win over France in the third-place match on Saturday night would never have played out like that if it was the final. An exciting World Cup as a whole does not guarantee a final of the same ilk. So, actually, this was a typical World Cup final, one to follow Germany 1-0 Argentina (after extra time, 2014), Spain 1-0 Netherlands (after extra time, 2010), Brazil 0-0 Italy (3-2 on pens, 1994).

Scholars of ancient Greek have been left scratching their heads at Christopher Nolan's “The Odyssey”, conflicted between accuracies and an increase in interest.

The latest adaptation of Homer’s epic poem had an epic debut, grossing $264.1 million in global ticket sales on its opening weekend, including $124.5 million in the U.S. and Canada, Universal Pictures said on Sunday.

The film, based on the ancient Greek poem by Homer, stars Matt Damon as the Greek hero Odysseus, and follows his perilous journey home after fighting the ⁠Trojan War. It is Nolan's first movie since the 2023 ​blockbuster "Oppenheimer," ⁠which won Academy Awards in several categories, including directing and best picture.

For Greek translator Emily Wilson, the release of the blockbuster has been gratifying in various ways. Her acclaimed 2017 edition of Homer's epic has reached the top 5 on Amazon.com, leading a wave of similar books boosted by the movie. Nolan has even cited her translation, notably the opening line “Tell me about a complicated man," as inspiration.

But the film itself, which opened this weekend and has received raves from many critics, left her unsatisfied.

“I want to celebrate the fact that so many more people are aware of 'The Odyssey' and were brought back to the poem,” she told The Associated Press. ”But at the same time, I had the sense that Christopher Nolan was trying to pack everything in while missing themes that were essential to the poem."

open image in gallery Stars of The Odyssey with director Christopher Nolan ( AP )

Reviewers have praised the acting and the narrative drive, the grand scale of a movie shot entirely on IMAX film and how it weds the sensibilities of ancient Greece and the modern world, at least as Nolan perceives it.

The divide between scholars and critics seems in part a matter of whether the balance should tilt toward Nolan or Homer. Wilson and fellow translator Daniel Mendelsohn both expressed admiration for Nolan's cinematic flair and ambition, what Mendelsohn calls his “great visual panache.” Both speculated that his desire to make a “Christopher Nolan” movie led to unfortunate decisions.

Mendelsohn is an author, critic and translator and his assessment appeared Friday in The New York Review of Books, where he is an editor-at-large.

Mendelsohn had previously defended Nolan's controversial decision to cast a Black actor, Lupita Nyong’o, as Helen of Troy, calling it a worthy way to “provoke, challenge and discomfit how we think about beauty and identity.” But he faulted the director for giving us an Odysseus with “no cleverness, no humor, no wily charm.” One of the Western canon's formative tricksters has been transformed, he contended, into the kind of haunted protagonist featured in such previous Nolan movies as “Oppenheimer” and “Memento.”

"This tormented, guilt-ridden Odysseus, stripped of humor and wit, seductiveness and cleverness, is a sibling of Memento’s anguished amnesiac, of Batman, of Oppenheimer, men tormented by pasts they wrestle with in different ways," wrote Mendelsohn, whose “Odyssey” translation came out in 2025. “Nolan has merely remade Homer’s hero in his own image.”

open image in gallery Matt Damon as Odysseus, left, and Zendaya as Athena, in a scene from ‘The Odyssey’ ( © Universal Studios. All Rights Reserved. )

Wilson, a professor of classical studies at the University of Pennsylvania, said she didn't want to come across as a “snobby,” nitpicking expert at odds with any deviation from the original text. But she questioned a range of omissions and other choices, from the absence on screen of the Gods Zeus and Poseidon (Athena is played by Zendaya ) to the “incoherent” messaging that condemns both war and physical cowardice. She found Penelope's role so thinned out that it endangered “any possibility of believing in this marriage.” Wilson also that thought parts of the movie, notably the scenes with Odysseus' dog, Argos, “catered towards modern sentimentality.”

“Everybody's a sucker for a dog,” she said.

A spokesperson for Nolan did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Wilson declined to offer a grade or ranking for the movie, but said she would recommend it for others, as long as they see it in a cinema.

“It was fun to be there with my kids. I didn’t feel it was pulling teeth to engage with it,” she said. “If you can see it on a big screen you should absolutely go."

President Donald Trump took in his first and only match of the World Cup after arriving at Sunday’s final to watch Argentina and Spain battle it out for the trophy.

The president briefly appeared on MetLife Stadium’s scoreboard screen, where he was seen standing in a secured area behind protective glass with FIFA’s president Gianni Infantino and first lady Melania Trump. There was no discernible reaction from the crowd, according to White House pool reporters.

A staffer held out the FIFA trophy for the president to inspect, which Trump patted before it was whisked away. He watched the remainder of the match from the box with Infantino as well as the Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.

His youngest son, Barron, was also in attendance, along with other Trump family members including his son Eric Trump and his wife Lara Trump, daughter Ivanka Trump and her husband Jared Kushner, and daughter Tiffany Trump and her husband Michael Boulos.

Trump said he would bring up the idea of hosting the championship again during a Friday press conference with Infantino. Hosting rights for the next two World Cups have already been decided. Trump and Infantino attended Sunday’s match together, and their friendship has added another political layer to the global tournament.

open image in gallery Donald Trump and Gianna Infantino attend the World Cup Final ( Reuters )

“It turned out we were a soccer country, and I think it’s going to remain,” Trump said Friday during an event at Trump Tower in New York. “This has really brought the world together.”

open image in gallery Trump, his wife Melania, and FIFA’s president listen to the National Anthem’s performance before Sunday’s game ( AFP/Getty )

Trump’s helicopter completed a brief flyover, which went largely unnoticed by the crowd, according to reporters in the stadium. Marine One then touched down outside the arena.

He also spoke to reporters on the Fox Sports pregame show ahead of Sunday’s game.

Trump is set to present the trophy to the winning team after the game. He isn’t outright backing Argentina, but he told Fox reporters earlier in the day: “It’s hard to bet against [Lionel] Messi.”

“I thought about it a lot. I knew that was a question. I hate to get involved, even though politically, it doesn't matter so much. The head of Argentina is a friend of mine, he’s done a terrific job. But I would say that it's hard to bet against Messi,” Trump told Fox’s Jenny Taft. “I won't pick sides. I just think it’s very hard to bet against Messi. He's great.”

At the game, his attention turned back to Washington matters momentarily. Shortly after arriving at the stadium, the posted twice on Truth Social, slamming former special counsel Jack Smith and a call from Democrats to expand the Supreme Court.

His attendance came amid a reignition of his administration’s war with Iran, with the two countries trading strikes over the weekend and news breaking a day earlier that two U.S. servicemembers were killed in an attack on a base in Jordan on Friday.

A third service member was killed Saturday after the controlled detonation of an unexploded Iranian drone, military officials announced Sunday.

open image in gallery Trump gave a pre-game shoutout to Lionel Messi ahead of Sunday's final ( Reuters )

He described his idea for helping FIFA avoid controversy by allowing the U.S. to host again in the near future, adding: “I had a great idea for Gianni.”

“I said: ‘You have to do two countries. So announce us for next time, and then announce another country after that and it’ll take out some of the anger and the shock!’ Now I think it’s a great idea,” Trump said. “Based on the numbers, we will be requesting it again immediately. I said, to take out the shock, you could announce another country for the next one... but we have to do this again.”

The president sparked anger among football (soccer) fans after he called on Infantino to overturn a referee’s red card against a player on the U.S. team before their elimination earlier this month.

That incident put a sour note over what has generally been a successful effort by the U.S. to host the World Cup, which played out in more than a dozen stadiums across the U.S., Canada and Mexico this year. Roughly 10 million people were projected to travel to the three countries to witness the games.t

The next FIFA World Cup tournament will be primarily hosted by Morocco, Portugal, and Spain, and the 2034 event will be held in Saudi Arabia.

The earliest the U.S. could conceivably host the next World Cup would be 2038, or nine years after Trump leaves office.

News.title: Hamilton takes out Russell as Antonelli stretches lead with Belgian GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from Spa-Francorchamps. The story of yesterday and in fact the weekend was of everyone trying to dislodge Kimi Antonelli from the top of the timesheets. Spoiler alert if you did not watch qualifying: they failed.

That is not to say the fight wasn’t a half-decent one. Max Verstappen and Red Bull were the closest challengers in the end, demonstrating an element of revival during a tricky season. Whether that will continue during the race is hard to know. Verstappen certainly thought he would have been further down the field without the tremendous tow he received from Isack Hadjar, his Red Bull team-mate, in the final sector.

Lando Norris also pushed Verstappen, though was almost half a second down on Antonelli’s time in the end. Unfortunately he will not be able to take advantage of a start from third place because he takes a 10-place grid penalty. George Russell, who has managed to reduce his Mercedes team-mate’s advantage to just 25 points in the past few rounds, was fourth and will start third. He did however, have a difficult session once again, finishing more than half a second off his team-mate.

He was at a loss to explain this. Well, he knows where he lost most of the time: on the straights. But he still does not understand exactly why it is happening. The good news for him is that third place is often the most optimal starting position at this track.

Will that be the case today? Let’s see...

News.title: Ryan Fox matches father Grant’s sporting folklore with Claret Jug
News.content:
It’s the final day of the Open Championship, golf’s oldest and most-prestigious major. The leaderboard offers up hope of a seesaw day where little-known-of golfers tussle it out with big names under the north-west English sun. All in all, it should be an exciting day.

But, as with the past two days, we head into the round with talk dominated by a certain Bryson DeChambeau. It’s as frustrating and annoying as it is, in these days dominated by social media/content etc etc, painfully predictable. So let’s get the DeChambeau news out the way. Having been fairly hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on Friday, the YouTube content creator had a tantrum, threatened to withdraw, caused a delay in the release of third-round tee times, before turning up and shooting a one-under 69 to lie four behind the leader heading into today.

That’s not all, The Bryson DeChambeau Show carried on after yesterday’s round where James Corrigan takes up the script...

Bryson DeChambeau marched straight to the offices of the R&A after being heckled with a cry of “you’re a cheat” on Birkdale’s 18th green on Saturday. As the controversy over his two-shot penalty from Friday’s second round rumbled on, Telegraph Sport understands DeChambeau, who shot a third-round 69 to lie four shots off the lead of the Open, asked R&A chief executive Mark Darbon for his scorecard from Friday. It is against policy so his request was rejected. DeChambeau then went back to the recorder’s hut and asked if they had it. Again, the answer was in the negative. It is unclear why he wanted it, but a theory emerged that he wished to put it on his social media channels.

All in all it is pathetic posturing that you’d expect from a stroppy teenager. He’s only three off the lead and has the game to win at Royal Birkdale, he’d do well to forget the perceived slights (whatever they may be) and get on with trying to win the Claret Jug.

Oh, and to add another scene to the soap opera Rory McIlroy doubtless spoke for many inside and outside the rope when he called out DeChambeau saying: “Yeah, look, I won’t pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I’m not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it’s for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.”

So, I think it’s best we focus on the golf today and not the theatrics and sorry antics of the American.

Sam Burns, his playing partner yesterday, was brilliant as he backed up his 62 of Friday with a five-under 65. He leads by two on 10 under and is the man to beat. Lurking behind with intent are a host of big names and big hitters – Ryan Fox (eight under), Si Woo Kim (eight under), Lucas Herbert (six under), Ludvig Aberg (seven under) and the man himself YouTube’s very own DeChambeau (six under).

Also in with a hint of a hope is Tommy Fleetwood, the hometown boy in search of his first major, the Englishman will start the round on five under.

Stay here for all the action, where I hope all the talk during and after the day’s round is focused on the winner’s brilliance rather than the emotions of DeChambeau.

News.title: Records tumble at Lord’s as England win thriller against India
News.content:
When he fell, bowled trying to sweep Bethell, India were 260 for two, still a tough ask but not impossible, especially against an England side with plenty of demons. Kohli fired up in Rohit’s absence, hitting Will Jacks for two sixes and Bethell into the pavilion.

But the run-rate faltered as Curran whipped out his slower-ball bag of tricks. He had Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer caught in the deep by sub Rehan Ahmed in the 44th over and Kohli in the next, slapping a catch to cover. The rest subsided, India short in the end at 360 for seven.

England’s ODI side have struggled for runs under Brendon McCullum and this was easily their best batting performance, not just for the collection of records but for the calm, controlled way they went about setting a huge total. The openers Duckett and Bethell gave them a 192-run cushion, Root was impregnable again and Buttler finished it off, proving what he can do when others give him a platform. India were without Jasprit Bumrah but that should not take the shine off England’s achievements.

This was the first Duckett-Bethell opening contribution and it was England’s highest for the first wicket since the last World Cup. Jason Roy and Jonny Bairstow were such an important part of the route to World Cup glory and they left a huge hole in the side. Duckett and Bethell are more touch players, capable of gear shifts rather than setting out at turbo pace like Roy and Bairstow. The fact they bat so often together in Test cricket, where Bethell appears at No 3, helps the level of understanding.

Duckett’s innings knocked Viv Richards’s 138 in the 1979 World Cup final off the top spot at Lord’s and continued the form he showed at the end of the New Zealand Test series when he scored his first Test hundred in nearly a year. He was out first ball in the second ODI in Cardiff but was never in any real bother at Lord’s as he compiled a fourth century in this format.

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

News.title: Hometown hero Tommy Fleetwood facing tough ask to end 57 years of Open hurt
News.content:
Never mind Bryson DeChambeau stomping around in the rough as he improved his lie, for so long this Open Saturday turned into Tommy Fleetwood walking in his Royal Birkdale wonderland as he enhanced the mood of seemingly everyone in attendance.

Alas, the fun could not last and, even though he still has a chance of becoming England’s first Open winner on English soil since 1969, that finish looked costly. Fifty-seven years of hurt and all that...

On five under, Fleetwood is in a tie for ninth, five off the lead held by Sam Burns, the American who, after a 65, is two clear of New Zealander Ryan Fox and South Korean Kim Si-woo. DeChambeau is alongside Swede Ludvig Aberg, in a tie for sixth on six under, after a 69.

He was heckled on the 18th because of the two-shot penalty he received on Friday night for “inadvertently improving his lie” on the fifth. “You’re a cheat, Bryson,” the fan shouted.

It was a sour point that was in no way in keeping with the mood of this Saturday that had been overwhelmingly positive. With Fleetwood as the focus, of course.

The enormous crowd cheered and sang and backed their fellow Merseysider all the way as Fleetwood launched his charge into contention at this Southport links which he would once sneak on as a child. His playing partner, Jon Rahm, was taken aback by the level of support.

“The best way I can explain it, it was so intense that, without meaning any disrespect I’m glad England didn’t win the semi-final [of the World Cup] because I would have been having a heck of a three days with the fans if they had been playing Spain in tomorrow’s final,” Rahm said.

Sports.title: Does the World Cup final go to extra time or penalties?
Sports.content:

Leaving fans with one question on their lips, is there extra-time and penalties available if required?

Does the World Cup final go to extra-time or penalties?

In knockout matches at the World Cup, including the final, a winner must be decided.



Unlike the group stage, where games end in a draw if they are level after 90 minutes, during the knockouts, it’s win or lose.

If the score is level at the end of normal time, the match goes to extra-time.



Extra-time is a 30-minute period consisting of two 15-minute halves.

If nothing separates the two teams after the additional spell, a penalty shootout will take place to decide which team will progress to the next round.

Sports.title: World Cup 2026: How many games do players miss for a red card and how many have there been?
Sports.content:
WORLD CUP 2026 will be the biggest in the tournament’s history, and promises some huge rule changes too.

WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Referees at the festival of football will be under more pressure than ever with the new rules adopted by FIFA.

SunSport brings you all the details on red cards at the World Cup this summer.



How many games do players miss for a red card?

If a player is sent off at any point of the tournament, they will miss their nation’s next match.

However, FIFA holds the right to extend the ban or add any other sanctions to the ban if they deem necessary.



This is similar to the Premier League where dangerous fouls can be given longer punishments.

Any player who sees red in their nation’s final match of the competition will have to miss the next official match.

For example, if someone is sent off in the World Cup final, the player will have to miss the next friendly or qualifier the nation plays after the tournament.

Players can now also be sent off for two controversial new reasons, including covering your mouth with your shirt and leaving the pitch in protest at a referee’s decision.

Sports.title: Why are Fifa giving out rings to the World Cup winners?
Sports.content:
FOR the first time ever, the winners of the World Cup will be presented with commemorative rings.

Spain and Argentina are currently facing off at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.



Along with the iconic trophy and gold medals, the winning team are also being handed special rings to symbolise their triumph.

Here is all you need to know about the new prize and how fans can get their hands on one.



Why are Fifa giving out rings to the World Cup winners?

Either Spanish or Argentine players will be handed rings while making their way to the podium to lift the World Cup.

The winners of the NFL Super Bowl, NBA and Major League Baseball all get rings instead of medals to go with the team’s trophy.



World Cup chiefs have decided to commemorate the tournament held in the US by dishing out rings as a bonus prize.

Fifa said they are “bringing one of the most most recognisable American sporting traditions to the global game”.

What is on the World Cup winners’ ring?

One side of the ring displays the World Cup trophy.

The other side will show the winning nation.



After the final, the players will be given replicas before being presented with the official customised ring at a later date.

How can fans get their own World Cup ring?

A total of 30 rings will be dished out to the players and coaches of the winning country.

But a further 1,996 will be available for fans to buy.

Each ring will be numbered, custom-fitted and delivered to the supporter with its own certificate of authenticity.

Fifa are yet to reveal how much they will cost and where they can be purchased from.

When the half-time whistle blew, players quickly left the field of play and it was a huge 27 minutes and 18 seconds until they returned, with the half-time show taking place.

As per the International Football Association Board rules, the half-time break should be no longer than 15 minutes, with the interval in breach of those rules.

‌



Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira, Gustavo Dudamel and BTS all performed in the half-time show, which was curated by Chris Martin from Coldplay. However, Rooney wasn't impressed.

Speaking on the BBC, Rooney said: "I'll be honest, mine (highlight) was when it finished. I like lot of those artists but I thought it was crap.

"I did, honestly. It just didn't get me going. I want the football to come back on. I like Burna Boy, I like Bieber, I like Shakira. That was flat."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Micah Richards, who picked the performances of Shakira and Burna Boy as his highlights, called former international team-mate Rooney “miserable” for his frank assessment.

With the conversation following an advert promoting the BBC, host Gabby Logan added: “I’ll tell you what else you get on the BBC: honest reviews”.

‌



FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced plans for the show – which was curated by Coldplay frontman Chris Martin – in March last year.

Fans were left shocked to see Madonna arrive into the stadium on a buggy with Brazilian legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho driving the cart.

One fan said: "Madonna, Ronaldo the Phenomenon, and Ronaldinho Gaúcho together - never thought I'd see this."

Sports.title: World Cup fans issue the same complaint about half-time show as Spain vs Argentina delayed
Sports.content:
World Cup fans issue the same complaint about half-time show as Spain vs Argentina delayed

The World Cup final between Spain and Argentina played host to an extended half-time break at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey as Coldplay, Justin Biber and Shakira took centre stage from Lionel Messi and co

View 3 Images The FIFA World Cup 2026 final half-time break lasted 27 minutes (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

World Cup final fans have fumed over the length of the half-time show at MetLife Stadium as Spain and Argentina were forced to take an extended break. The finalists were forced to wait a massive 27minutes and 18 seconds to return to the field.

‌



In an unprecedented move, FIFA's showpiece event saw a planned break that extended beyond the traditional 15 minutes. The show itself, comprising the likes of Madonna, Justin Bieber, Shakira and K-pop band BTS, was expected to be 11 minutes long with additional time required to set up and take down the performance infrastructure.

‌



World football's governing body declined to clarify how long the interval at this year's World Cup final would be on multiple occasions. But, after backlash over the possibility of a 30-minute break, the intention was for the break to last a total of 17 minutes.

‌



Safe to say, the break was too long for most fans, even in a match that was harder to watch than most.

"This is actually disgraceful I cant lie," said one fan on social media. Another said: "Horrendously long half time show that nobody cares to watch btw @FIFA do better"

Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony READ MORE :

Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"I much preferred football when it was a game of two halfs and half-time was barely long enough for the manager to swear at the players and throw teacups round the dressing room," added another.

"I hope with this really long half time, there won’t be another hydration break…" pleaded a further fan. "This half time show is over the top and too long. When is the second half starting?!" said another.

Coldplay's Chris Martin curated the performance, which also featured Nigerian singer Burna Boy, Philharmonic director Gustavo Dudamel, and PS22 Chorus featuring Coldplay. The likes of Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal were forced into an extended break in New Jersey.

‌



View 3 Images Ronaldinho, Madonna and Ronaldo started the half-time show (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

The BBC and ITV were initially not going to broadcast the show and planned to focus on the highlights and analysis from the opening 45 minutes. However, with the break extended, it was deemed possible to broadcast analysis and the on-pitch exploits at the break.

Gary Neville found something to like about the show. Speaking on ITV, he said: "I quite enjoyed it, let's hope the second half picks up and there's loads of energy in that."

‌



On BBC, Wayne Rooney's verdict was less kind. "I'll be honest, mine (highlight) was when it finished," he said.

View 3 Images Justin Bieber performs (Image: Getty Images)

"I like lot of those artists but I thought it was crap. I did, honestly. It just didn't get me going. I want the football to come back on. I like Burna Boy, I like Bieber, I like Shakira. That was flat."

Article continues below

Last summer, FIFA also saw an extended break for the Club World Cup final. They flaunted the rules regarding the length of time between halves for the clash between Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain where the interval stretched to 25 minutes.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez suffered a cruel injury blow during the first half of the World Cup final

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez was in tears after being forced off with an injury in the World Cup final against Spain (Image: (Photo by Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images))

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez was spotted in floods of tears after being forced off the pitch during the World Cup final against Spain. The 28-year-old started the final in the heart of defence alongside Tottenham Hotspur defender Cristian Romero, but had to be replaced just before the half-time interval with an injury.

‌



It was a tight, nervy first half display from both teams, though Spain looked the most likely to score with Argentina failing to register a single shot inside the opening 45 minutes. Marc Cucurella had just curled an effort just wide of Emi Martinez's goal in the 43rd minute, when Martinez hit the floor.

‌



The United defender had been booked for a late foul on Mikel Oyarzabal just moments earlier, for stopping a Spanish counter attack in its tracks. However, 'The Butcher' was unable to continue and was replaced by former Manchester City defender Nicolas Otamendi in the 44th minute.

‌



Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite READ MORE :

Gary Lineker makes instant England prediction after France and responds to Bukayo Saka READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Martinez left the pitch in tears after being unable to carry on. The former United defender was consoled by Martinez before making his way off the pitch.

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez is consoled by Emi Martinez before he is replaced in the World Cup final vs Spain (Image: (Photo by Hector Vivas - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

‌



The United defender has been a mainstay in the Argentina defence en route to the final, but was visibly distraught after making his way off. He was seen crying, with his head in his hands on the bench.

Argentina were second best throughout the first half, with Spain boasting 65 per cent possession, registering three shots, two of which came on target.

The European champions got off to a fast start when Lamine Yamal burst into the box just five minutes into the game. The Barcelona winger tried to cross into the box, but the ball fell to Dani Olmo on the edge of the area.

‌



The Barca playmaker found Yamal in acres of space inside the 18-yard box, driving to the byline and trying to pick out the bottom corner.

However, a combination of both Lisandro Martinez and Emi Martinez kept the young Spanish star at bay.

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez's World Cup final participation was cut short (Image: BBC Sport)

Article continues below

Argentina were content to sit behind the ball with Lionel Messi as their sole man in attack. Spain kept probing and Oyarzabal called Martinez into action again in the 39th minute.

Fabian Ruiz poked the ball through to the Spanish striker, who rifled a first time left-footed effort down low into the corner, but Martinez was equal to it, keeping the score locked at 0-0 at the half-time interval.

Sports.title: Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite
Sports.content:
Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite

Donald Trump was booed by fans at the 2026 World Cup final at MetLife Stadium just seconds after the national anthem

View 2 Images U.S. President Donald Trump was booed by fans inside the Met Life Stadium at the World Cup final (Image: (Photo by Eva Marie Uzcategui - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Argentina and Spain fans made their feelings about Donald Trump crystal clear in booing the United States president when he appeared on the big screen at the World Cup Final. Trump had not attended the World Cup until the final, which caused a major headache for those attending the game.

‌



Federal agents, local law enforcement and private security firms had reportedly been mapping out Sunday's security operation for approximately two years, expecting the president to attend the tournament's showpiece event. However, technical problems meant scores of spectators and members of the media faced long delays getting into MetLife Stadium as measures were put in place following Trump's decision to attend.

‌



This, combined with his involvement with FIFA and Folarin Balogun's red card suspension being overturned, resulted in a mixed reception.

‌



Gary Lineker makes instant England prediction after France and responds to Bukayo Saka READ MORE :

Donald Trump picks his World Cup winner and makes request to Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Shortly before kick-off, just seconds after the national anthem concluded, Trump appeared on the giant screens inside MetLife Stadium.

The cheers that had accompanied the anthem quickly gave way to a chorus of boos, whistles, and jeers directed at the president, who had arrived via the Marine One helicopter and made a dramatic flyover of MetLife Stadium before the match got under way.

‌



Trump had been keen to avoid a repeat of his viral New York Knicks moment, while security teams left absolutely nothing to chance. F-16 fighter jets, military marksmen, and thousands of FBI agents were deployed to safeguard MetLife Stadium and the surrounding airspace.

The match has been designated a "Level 1" special event - the highest security classification in the US - putting it on a par with presidential inaugurations and State of the Union addresses.

View 2 Images United States President Donald Trump was booed (Image: Getty Images)

‌



A strictly enforced no-fly zone will cover the New York and New Jersey area from Friday through to Sunday's World Cup final, with snipers stationed on stadium rooftops and a heavily fortified perimeter set to cause considerable delays for supporters.

Once the final whistle blows and either Spain or Argentina are crowned champions, Trump is expected to hand over the iconic World Cup trophy to the victorious captain alongside FIFA president Gianni Infantino.

The 80-year-old was part of the celebrations when Chelsea lifted the trophy after beating Paris Saint-Germain in the Club World Cup Final last summer.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Trump and Infantino have cultivated a remarkably close bond - unlike anything previously witnessed between a FIFA president and a world leader - which culminated in the extraordinary inaugural awarding of the FIFA Peace Prize last December at the World Cup draw.

Ahead of the World Cup Final, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt defended the sheer scale of the security operation, framing Trump's attendance as the crowning moment of the entire tournament.

Article continues below

"His attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure and most successful World Cup in American history," Leavitt said.

Sports.title: 'My hands were all over the place!' - Fox savours dramatic Open win
Sports.content:
Ryan Fox admitted it was a "dream come true" as he defied the nerves to clinch a dramatic victory in The Open at Royal Birkdale.

The 39-year-old New Zealander produced a superb finish to the final round to overtake clubhouse leader Cameron Young and snatch a one-shot win.

Fox, who had carded a 62 on Saturday to put himself in contention to claim a maiden major success, looked to be slipping out of it after making his second bogey of the day at the 11th.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the final round of the 154th Open as Fox claimed the victory

Back-to-back birdies at the 13th and 14th put him back in the hunt and he then did well to escape with only a bogey at the 15th after a nightmare lie in a greenside bunker.

He hit back by birdieing the 16th following a brilliant approach and then, after missing a chance at the 17th, nailed two superb shots down the 18th before boldly draining a 12-foot putt to claim the Claret Jug.

"To play that last hole how I did, I stood on the tee and said to my caddie Dean (Smith), we're going to try to win this," said Fox.

"I hit two perfect shots. I'm not sure how I hit the putt. My hands were all over the place. I was just trying to get it towards the hole somewhere. It's surreal that it went in.

"My focus with the putter all day was just take a really deep breath before I hit it and just try to hit a line, and I did that.

Image: Fox celebrates after holing the winning putt

"I don't know how I managed to keep the putter face square enough for that to go on line, but I'll take it.

"Champion Golfer of the Year has got a pretty good ring to it. It is a dream come true.

"You do dream of this moment. I don't know whether I ever thought it was going to become a reality. Now it is, and to have my name etched in the history of the game is pretty awesome. I think it's pretty awesome for New Zealand as well. It's going to be big down there."

Fox is the son of former All Blacks fly-half Grant Fox and the grandson of former New Zealand Test captain Merv Wallace.

"We've got a great history in our family," he said. "I was lucky enough to carve my own path there. I don't know if this tops their achievements, but it's certainly right up there.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fox equalled the lowest round in Open history with a third-round 62 at Royal Birkdale

"I spoke to my kids last night, and they said bring back a trophy. I think this is a pretty cool one to bring back for them.

"I don't know if my dad would be able to contain himself when I was coming down the stretch. He's never been one who has been very good if he doesn't have control over things.

"I think when he was playing and in control of the output, under pressure he was fine. But when he doesn't have control, I think he's a nervous wreck. I'm sure he was."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player How Fox clinched victory in The Open at Royal Birkdale

'He stayed aggressive'

Sky Sports Golf duo Dame Laura Davies and Andrew Coltart were both full of praise for Fox and the aggressive approach he adopted on the back nine.

Davies said: "He was the most impressive player all day. He stayed aggressive; I don't think he was scared of losing it. If he lost it because he hit a shot that just didn't work out he was prepared to stay aggressive and I firmly believe that's why he did it.

"He hit irons when he had to, but when there was a chance, a sniff of a birdie, the driver was out, full commitment.

"And the way he played 18 I don't think you could have drawn that up any better. Two of the best shots he will ever hit in his life just to hit that green to give himself a chance."

Image: Fox proudly holds the Claret Jug

Coltart added: "I've never seen somebody push through the tape as hard as that right at the end of the tournament to win a major championship.

"At a place like this, too. It was just superb. The 62 on Saturday I think, helped cement his belief in his ability out there.

"While they all struggled with the pressure, he stood tall."

What's next?

The next PGA Tour event is the 3M Open at TPC Twin Cities in Minnesota, beginning Thursday, with early coverage on Sky Sports+ before switching to Sky Sports Golf at 7pm.

The 3M Open is part of a triple-header of live golf on Sky Sports, with the ISPS Handa Senior Open and ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open also live. The women's major season then concludes with the AIG Women's Open from July 30-August 2, also live on Sky Sports Golf. Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract.

Sports.title: 'My heart really sank' - Hamilton relieved mechanic unhurt after hit
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says his "heart really sank" when his Ferrari hit a mechanic in a pit-stop incident that led to the team being fined heavily by Belgian Grand Prix stewards.

Hamilton's right-front tyre struck the mechanic - who was unhurt - after the driver was given the green signal to leave the team's pit box, briefly knocking the crew member, who was in front of the wheel in an attempt to make a front-wing adjustment, to his knees.

Hamilton promptly stopped his car as the mechanic was helped to his feet, before leaving the pit box.

The incident was placed under a post-race stewards' investigation with Ferrari later handed a €30,000 fine, €10,000 of which is suspended for a year.

Ferrari admitted to an "inappropriately late instruction for the wing adjustment, a lack of clear communication and the mechanic's failure to notice the green light" amid a "complex and unusual combination of circumstances" at a stop which Hamilton had first served a five-second penalty before work on the car commenced.

With no fault attributed to the driver, who stewards said had also suffered a "sporting disadvantage" anyway due to the fact he was delayed in leaving the pit stop, Hamilton retained his fourth-place finish in the race.

The result moved Hamilton back into second place ahead of George Russell in the Drivers' Championship with a deficit of 45 points to Kimi Antonelli, the race winner at Spa-Francorchamps.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix

Speaking about the pit stop confusion after the race, Hamilton said his mind had immediately flashed back to an incident at the 2018 Bahrain Grand Prix when a botched Ferrari stop for Kimi Raikkonen caused a mechanic, Francesco Cigarini, to suffer a double leg fracture.

Hamilton was therefore relieved to be told that the mechanic involved on Sunday was not injured, when he enquired about him over team radio.

"The green light went and so I went," said Hamilton to Sky Sports F1.

"You're looking over here [to the left at the lights] you're not looking over there so that's more probably on the team, ultimately.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Despite being given a five-second penalty for an opening lap collision with George Russell, Lewis Hamilton was left more frustrated with his performance over the weekend as he finished fourth in Belgium

"But when it happened, then I noticed him and I stopped and it just went through my mind in that moment was back when Kimi hit and [a mechanic] broke a leg and my heart really sank for a second.

"I'm really grateful he's OK."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton crashes at Turn 13 during the final practice session at the Belgian GP

'We could have been challenging for the win' - Hamilton rues consequence of his Saturday crash

Hamilton's stop had already been elongated by the fact that Ferrari's crew had first had to wait five seconds before starting the car's tyre change owing to the serving of a time penalty for causing a collision with Russell at Les Combes on the opening lap.

The clash spun Russell out of the race, although the Mercedes driver later blamed his own car's straight-line speed issues, rather than former team-mate Hamilton, for the incident at the end of the long Kemmel Straight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton

Hamilton also preferred not to focus on the specifics of the collision in his post-race interview, instead taking the blame for not qualifying higher than sixth, which became fifth on the grid due to Lando Norris' engine penalty, after crashing in Saturday's final practice session.

"I don't count on myself [being] unlucky, I think about my mistake that I made yesterday, so I take full responsibility really for the fourth place that I ended up getting," he said.

"I damaged the car then when they rebuilt the car they missed something on the suspension so the balance was completely different so it meant I was probably a good couple of tenths - maybe three tenths - slower than I should have been in qualifying.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Drama at the start of the Belgium GP as George Russell's title hopes take a huge blow

"Then I ended up further back, got in the incident. Five second penalty, so like a domino effect from a mistake from myself.

"But the team have been doing a great job with strategy, pit stops. We are continuing to improve the car. I think our pace today, without the damage, we could have been challenging for the win."

Sports.title: Antonelli takes big Belgian GP win as Russell's title woes deepen
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli overcame an unfortunately-timed Virtual Safety Car to overtake Charles Leclerc and win the Belgian Grand Prix on a day team-mate George Russell's title hopes suffered a major fresh setback.

Antonelli doubled his in-house advantage over Russell to 50 points after the Briton was spun out into the gravel at the fifth corner of the first lap in a collision with Lewis Hamilton that stewards judged the Ferrari driver at fault for.

Hamilton was given a five-second penalty, which he served at his sole pit stop, and eventually finished fourth after overtaking McLaren's Oscar Piastri with four laps to go.

Hamilton and Ferrari faced a post-race investigation for an unsafe Ferrari release at the same pit stop.

A mechanic was struck by the Ferrari's front-right tyre and was briefly knocked to his knees after Hamilton was incorrectly given the signal to leave his pit box. The mechanic was unhurt.

Ferrari were fined €30,000, of which a third of the amount was suspended for 12 months, for the incident.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ferrari pit crew were unable to adjust Lewis Hamilton's front wing as the British driver knocked over a mechanic after being given the green light

Hamilton moves back ahead of Russell to second behind Antonelli in the standings - 45 points behind the Italian, whose sixth victory of the season reinforces his championship favourite status with one race to go in Hungary this coming week before Formula 1's summer break after Mercedes unreliability had struck his car in two of the previous three races.

Max Verstappen, who briefly took the lead from Antonelli on the first lap into Eau Rouge before the Mercedes almost immediately blasted back past, took third after he was also jumped by Leclerc during the VSC.

The Dutchman struggled on the hard tyres in the final stint and finished nine seconds behind Leclerc for Red Bull's 300th podium finish in F1.

Isack Hadjar drove strongly to finish sixth in the second Red Bull from the back row, opportunistically making two pit stops under the early Safety Car for Russell's crash to fulfil the mandatory race-tyre requirements.

Hadjar just held off Lando Norris, who was on significantly fresher tyres, after the McLaren had run to lap 30 before making his one pit stop having started a penalised 13th on the grid.

Gabriel Bortoleto was eighth for Audi ahead of Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Franco Colapinto.

Belgian GP Result: Top 10 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



3) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



4) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



5) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



6) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



7) Lando Norris, McLaren



8) Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi



9) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls



10) Franco Colapinto, Alpine

How faultless Antonelli was made to win the hard way

Mercedes' world championship leader had been the big favourite to win the race after qualifying on a dominant pole position but the 19-year-old's route to victory on Sunday did not prove quite as straightforward as many had expected across a tense 44 laps of racing at Spa-Francorchamps.

Antonelli had, though, always been braced for a battle to hold on to his lead through the first lap of the race from fellow front-row-starter Verstappen due to the slipstream-friendly nature of the opening part of the undulating, power-sensitive Belgian lap.

He stayed ahead on the short initial run to La Source but, amid different stages of energy deployment, was overtaken by Verstappen as they arrived at the bottom of Eau Rouge.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Drama at the start of the Belgium GP as George Russell's title hopes take a huge blow

But Antonelli had more battery power in hand for the long Kemmel Straight and duly breezed straight back past the Red Bull before the next braking zone of Les Combes.

Leclerc, meanwhile, had made an impressive start from fourth place and passed Verstappen too.

Verstappen got back ahead of the Ferrari for second place on lap six and, impressively so given the pre-race expectations had been that Antonelli would run and hide, managed to keep the leading Mercedes in view. He was less than three seconds behind Antonelli when he pitted first on lap 17.

Antonelli stopped a lap later and stayed ahead of the Red Bull to maintain the net race lead.

But Ferrari had kept both their drivers out for longer and benefitted when, on lap 20, the Virtual Safety Car was initiated for debris on track.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Kimi Antonelli discusses his Belgian GP win and admits he's in a 'good position' after opening up a 45-point gap in the drivers' standings.

With the cars on circuit forced to run at reduced speed, Ferrari were able to pit their drivers simultaneously while losing less race time compared to a non-VSC stop.

It worked a treat as Leclerc had jumped both Verstappen and Antonelli on his return to the circuit.

However, Hamilton, who first had to serve his five-second penalty before his tyre change could commence, was further delayed when confusion led to the mechanic who had been asked to adjust his front wing being knocked over when the Briton incorrectly got the green light to leave the box.

Leclerc re-emerged 2.5 seconds ahead of Antonelli and with the apparent advantage of slightly fresher hard tyres.

But the Mercedes simply had too much speed and, unlike two weeks before at Silverstone when the Silver Arrow ran into technical trouble just as it appeared poised to overtake the Ferrari for the lead, Antonelli on lap 34 moved ahead of Leclerc down the Kemmel Straight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri takes to his McLaren team radio to complain about contact with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

Not that Mercedes simply breezed away from Ferrari thereafter, Antonelli eventually taking the chequered flag just 1.9s ahead of Leclerc to secure a narrow but significant win given the context of both his recent misfortune and Russell's early exit here.

"It's great to be back on the top step after obviously a few difficult rounds," said Antonelli. "It was a hard-fought race. We lost first place with a VSC but then we managed to make our way back.

"It was a tough win because Charles was quick and we had to hold onto them."

Second place followed Leclerc's victory at Silverstone amid a resurgence in his form, and the Monegasque said: "I believed in the win until the end. We had a little bit of luck with the VSC at the right time for us but the pace was relatively strong.

"There were five or six laps on the hard tyres when I was struggling with the front axle, then it came back a little bit."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell pointed to an issue with the car as a reason for his collision with Lewis Hamilton during the Belgian GP

Russell bemoans Mercedes straight-line speed issues after Hamilton tangle

Race day could barely have gone any worse for a frustrated Russell in the other title-contending Mercedes car.

The Briton had qualified third, a position he held until the Kemmel Straight on lap one when both Ferraris drafted past him and he came under attack from Piastri's McLaren too.

Russell attempted to come back at Hamilton on the outside of his compatriot under braking for the right-handed turn into Les Combes, but the Ferrari understeered and tagged the Mercedes' right-rear wheel, spinning it round into the gravel.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton.

Stewards may have penalised Hamilton for the incident, but Russell instead took issue with the mysterious straight-line speed issues that had dogged his Mercedes all weekend.

"I just got totally swallowed up down the straight," said a dejected Russell.

"I lost three positions down the straight down into Turn Five and then the incident was a racing incident.

"Maybe I could have gone a bit wider, maybe he (Hamilton) could have braked a bit more. The incident shouldn't have happened if I had the speed down the straight."

Sports.title: England clinch India series in Lord's run-fest
Sports.content:
Ben Duckett's century and Sam Curran's late burst of wickets inspired England to a series-clinching 27-run win over India in the third ODI at Lord's.

Duckett struck a magnificent 141 from 135 balls, the highest individual ODI score at Lord's and his fourth century in the format, before a swashbuckling 41 from just 13 balls by Jos Buttler helped England set India a daunting 388 to win.

Rohit Sharma led the chase with a superb 138 off 110 deliveries, registering his 34th ODI hundred and sharing century partnerships with Shubman Gill (77) and Virat Kohli (74) to keep India firmly on course.

England vs India, third ODI, Lord’s England 387-3 after 50 overs (chose to bat): Ben Duckett (141 off 135), Jacob Bethell (91 off 93), Joe Root (74 off 48), Jos Buttler (41 off 13); Prasidh Krishna (2-69), Prince Yadav (1-79) India 260-7 after 50 overs: Rohit Sharma (138 off 110), Shubman Gill (77 off 84), Virat Kohli (74 off 60); Sam Curran (4-75), Jacob Bethell (1-49), Jofra Archer (1-63) Adil Rashid (1-64)

India were 303-2 and needed 84 from the final 39 balls when a decisive seven-ball spell saw Curran (4-75) dismiss Ishan Kishan (14), Shreyas Iyer (0) and Kohli, halting India's momentum as their chase fell 27 runs short.

After losing the series opener by six wickets at Edgbaston, England bounced back to secure a 2-1 ODI series victory over the world's top-ranked side, adding it to their 4-0 T20 series whitewash of India.

How England clinched ODI series victory over India

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Duckett puts on a dominant display against India as he bats an amazing 141

Harry Brook completed a clean sweep of successful tosses with his third of the series, and his decision to bat paid immediate dividends as England's openers feasted on an Indian attack left rudderless without injured pace talisman Jasprit Bumrah.

India were made to toil in the field as England recorded a record 192-run first-wicket stand before Bethell picked out Rohit Sharma at cow corner to fall nine runs short of an emotional century on the day Lord's remembered Sir Garfield Sobers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jacob Bethell is dismissed for 90 as he bats a superb innings in England's third ODI match against India

Duckett kicked on after reaching his century, blasting 18 fours and a six to surpass Sir Viv Richards' 138 not out against England in 1979 and register a new highest individual score in a Lord's ODI before falling caught and bowled to Prince Yadav.

Joe Root hit a sixth successive ODI half-century after Duckett's dismissal before Jos Buttler's four fours and three sixes in a blistering late cameo saw England plunder 82 runs from the final five overs to finish on 387-3 after 50 overs of domination with the bat.

It left India needing to pull off the second-highest run chase in ODI history to win the series, but confidence grew that it could be possible when Rohit and Gill put on a 147-run opening stand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Duckett puts on a dominant display against India as he bats an amazing 141

Gill suffered a recurrence of the cramp that forced him to retire in the first ODI at Edgbaston, and four overs after receiving treatment the India captain was trapped lbw as Adil Rashid claimed a crucial breakthrough with his first wicket of the series.

Rohit sealed his eighth ODI century on English soil from 84 balls in a 113-run stand with Kohli, as the two legendary Indian batsmen sought a thrilling final chapter in what may prove to be their final international appearances in England.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rohit Sharma reaches a century in India’s 3rd ODI match against England

Bethell (1-49) bowled Rohit, delivering the crucial breakthrough to reduce India to 260-2, but Kohli's first fifty at Lord's in any format kept the tourists on track.

But Curran's late brilliance derailed the India chase as they were restricted to 360-7 from 50 overs, with England claiming a fifth win from six matches and only their second ODI series victory over India since 2012.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sam Curran takes three wickets in quick succession against India

'Proud' Brook savours series win

England captain Harry Brook:

"I am extremely proud. We fought hard, communicated well like we did in the T20s and have managed to scrape a series win against the world No 1 team.

"We want to set a template with the bat and the way Ben Duckett and Jacob Bethell started with the bat was phenomenal.

"To be no wickets down after 30 overs and not look like they were taking a risk."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England captain Harry Brook reflects on England’s ODI series victory over India and what it means to the team

Gill rues England's late-innings runs

India captain Shubman Gill:

"I think we were right in the game up until the 45th over [of England's innings]. We gave up too many runs in the last three overs and that's where the game went too far out from us.

"We thought if we had wickets in hand after 40 overs, we would be in the game. After the powerplay, we tried to get the required run rate down."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Shubman Gill was dismissed for 77 as India continue to battle back against England in the 3rd ODI

Root: England developing as ODI side

Player of the Series, Joe Root (249 runs in three games and never dismissed):

"To bounce back from our defeat in the first ODI and beat the No 1 side is the most rewarding thing.

"To back up a brilliant series win in Sri Lanka with this shows we are going in the right direction in a really positive way.

"It is great to see the guys developing and learning."

Sports.title: 'I reached rock bottom' - Antonelli admits shock as title charge accelerates
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has admitted he could not have imagined being in a dominant position at the top of the Formula 1 world championship 12 months ago when he reached "rock bottom" during his rookie campaign.

Antonelli, 19, won the Belgian Grand Prix for Mercedes on Sunday to move 45 points clear of Lewis Hamilton at the top of the drivers' standings, with 10 of 22 currently scheduled rounds complete.

Having been fast-tracked in by Mercedes boss Toto Wolff to replace Hamilton following the seven-time world champion's decision to join Ferrari, Antonelli endured a chastening spell midway through his 2025 campaign.

The then 18-year-old went on a dismal run during which he finished above ninth just once in 10 grands prix, with one of the low points coming as he was knocked out in Q1 in Belgium last year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli discusses his Belgian GP win and admits he's in a 'good position' after opening up a 45-point gap in the drivers' standings

Asked after claiming his sixth victory of the season on Sunday whether he could have imagined this scenario a year ago, Antonelli replied: "No, absolutely not.

"Last year here, I probably reached the bottom, so it was a very difficult weekend for me mentally.

"But this year was definitely a lot better. If you had asked me last year at this moment, I probably would have said no."

Antonelli's advantage at the top of the standings could actually be far greater if it were not for a spell of bad luck the Italian has endured in recent weeks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli wins the Belgian Grand Prix

He suffered an engine failure when running second to Hamilton in Barcelona, and then suffered a wheel-guard failure that dropped him out of the points at the British Grand Prix when he appeared to be on course to chase Charles Leclerc down for victory.

His pace dominance over his team-mate George Russell, who began the year as the clear title favourite, makes it hard to see how Antonelli can be caught unless Ferrari make major improvements to their inferior power unit in the near future.

Despite his strong position, Antonelli is not dwelling on the increasing likelihood of him becoming by far the youngest driver to become an F1 world champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli joins Sky Sports' Karun Chandhok at the SkyPad to analyse the Italian's pole-setting lap at the Belgian Grand Prix

"I never want to relax too much," Antonelli told Sky Sports F1.

"Of course, it's a great result and good redemption after last year because last year was a very dark moment for me and to get the win is very special.

"But you can never relax because we have seen in the past how the situation can swing so quickly.

"So that's why it's important to really maximise and take every opportunity that is given, and just make the best out of it because you never know what can happen."

Wolff: We're all surprised by Antonelli form

Wolff made the decision to give Antonelli one of the most desirable seats on the grid when several other strong options were available, and there were times during 2025 when the choice came under great scrutiny.

While Wolff says Antonelli's ups and downs during his debut campaign were expected, the Austrian admits the teenager's remarkable consistency in 2026 has "surprised" the whole team.

"We're all surprised", Wolff said. "I think the first season came as expected. Great moments where his talent shined through, and then moments which were very difficult - the long spell of lack of results in the middle of the season, as expected.

"And then after the winter, also as expected, he knew the environment, he knew the pressures, he knew the demands of the team on the technical side, on the marketing side, knowing the tracks that we would go racing.

"But what was not expected is the serenity and structure that he brought into his game. With Kimi, whether the session was good or bad, you wouldn't see a difference in emotions in the debrief.

"It is absolutely transactional. What is the problem? How do we solve it? How do we move on? And that is new. And I think that's why it's almost when he wins, you can't see this absolute excitement that a 19-year-old would almost have."

Wolff highlighted Antonelli's reactions to the reliability issues that cost him in Barcelona and at Silverstone as further examples of his protégé's level-headedness.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli suffers damage during the British Grand Prix

Wolff added: "And at the same time, when he fails to deliver results, in Barcelona, when we had the car stoppage, or even in Silverstone, he comes back in and he was the one saying to the team, 'this is a mechanical sport, these things can happen'.

"Nineteen-years-old - that is very impressive to see. And I think this mindset and this attitude is probably one of the main drivers that has allowed the talent to shine so early in his career."
