Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez SENT OFF in World Cup final for Argentina - as Wayne Rooney hits out at Chelsea midfielder for 'silly' challenge
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez SENT OFF in World Cup final for Argentina - as Wayne Rooney hits out at Chelsea midfielder for 'silly' challenge

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the 93rd minute of regular time in the World Cup final, leaving Argentina in the lurch.

The Chelsea midfielder was given a second yellow card for a late challenge on Spain defender Pau Cubarsi by the halfway line and dismissed with minutes to go before extra-time.

He protested his innocence vehemently - as did his team-mates Lionel Messi and Facundo Medina - but it was hard to argue against the decision of referee Slavko Vincic. Cubarsi had gone flying through the air after the foul.

Wayne Rooney said on the BBC: 'A silly tackle. He's a little bit late to it. On a yellow card you can't just dangle your leg out. It makes it a very different game now.'

Fernandez's dismissal rounded off an abysmal 90 minutes for the 2022 champions, who had no shots compared to Spain's 15.

His team-mate Leandro Paredes was perhaps lucky to avoid a second yellow moments after for a foul on the edge of the box as Argentina continued their vicious style of play.

Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the 93rd minute for a very late challenge on Pau Cubarsi

The midfielder had the brass neck to complain about being given a second yellow, but he didn't have much of a leg to stand on

Lamine Yamal tested the goalkeeper Lisandro Martinez from that free-kick but La Albiceleste held on to force an additional 30 minutes at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

Messi, who has eight goals at the World Cup, was largely anonymous throughout regular time.

Fernandez has proven a crucial player at the heart of midfield for Lionel Scalino throughout the campaign.

The 25-year-old ironically scored a 93rd-minute winner in the last 16 against Egypt and netted Argentina's equaliser against England in the semi-finals.

Spain came flying out of the blocks in extra-time and substitute Nico Williams thought he had put Spain ahead after the restart, but the goal was ruled out for a foul, seemingly for a dubious one on Nicolas Otamendi.

Fans in the stadium began to chant 'Infantino' after that, feeling that the FIFA president has rigged the tournament in Argentina's favour.

The last time Argentina had a man sent off in a World Cup final was in 1990, when they had two players given their marching orders.

Pedro Monzon and Gustavo Dezotti were sent off that day in a 1-0 defeat by West Germany.

The match is ongoing. More to follow.

Sports.title: The great World Cup final 'rip-off'! Fans poke fun at offering for supporters who paid $1m for top hospitality tickets
Sports.content:
The great World Cup final 'rip-off'! Fans poke fun at offering for supporters who paid $1m for top hospitality tickets

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A hospitality provider has come under fire for the offering it has provided for supporters at the World Cup final.

Ahead of the tournament's showpiece event, 10 fans secured a $1million (£743,640) package through On Location, a company that describes itself as 'the official hospitality partner for the world's premier sports, music, and lifestyle events'.

Yet when photos of the pitch side seats those 10 ticket-holders had at the New York New Jersey Stadium were shared by Sports Business Journal reporter Alex Silverman, many were quick to hit out.

One social media user said: 'All that to sit on a polyester Amazon couch...'

Another added: 'This is the worst thing I've read for a while. I despise so much of this Americanised tournament.'

A further shocked fan quipped: '$1m? For the worst seats? Who the f*** wants to sit there?'

Fans have hit out at the pitch side seats given to fans who paid $1m for a World Cup final ticket

The fact they were sitting on sofas and facing the sun was one heavily debated issue

An extra user chipped in with: 'Why would someone even pay that much,' before another supporter said: 'Pitch side views are the worst view in every football stadium on the globe. They have all been royally shafted here.'

Meanwhile, with the game starting at 3PM local time and the temperature at around 27 degrees centigrade, the sun was shining.

All of the supporters were subsequently given special sun hats to deal with the conditions, while they appeared to just be sitting on a regular sofa and behind a glass barrier, issues that further attracted the ire of social media users.

One said: '$1 million and it's genuinely a terrible view,' before another said: 'Glad they threw the hat in there for free given the price, wouldn't have been worth it otherwise.'

A third wrote: 'And you get an obstructed view with the photographer standing in front of you the whole game.'

Despite the furore over the quality of seats, it must be noted that the $1million package does reportedly include several other supposed perks for the lucky fans.

The whole experience was said to start on Saturday when the ticket-holders attended a Sports Illustrated party that was hosted by 50 Cent and Diplo.

They were then transported from Manhattan to the New York New Jersey Stadium via helicopter, while other VIP tickets to high profile events and restaurants for after the World Cup final were also thrown in.

Daily Mail Sport contacted On Location for comment.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney was spot on about the NAUSEATING World Cup final half-time show. It was another symbol of Gianni Infantino's FIFA vanity project - and proper fans would have booed it, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
Anyway, that’s quite enough of Gary Neville, Ian Wright and Roy Keane chatting about the footy on ITV. Because Madonna is here, miming her 2000 hit ‘Music’, in a jeep being driven by Ronaldo and Ronaldinho, heading into the MetLife Stadium in the shadows of New York City.

Watched over by our curator, Chris Martin AKA Coldplay, it was all so spectacularly tacky, involving Shakira, BTS, Burna Boy and Justin Bieber tempting us towards sleep with a haunting ballad. Kermit the Frog and Miss Piggy sang something a little more upbeat at least – insert muppet joke about our footballing overlord Gianni Infantino here – but their vibes alone will not have stopped a few million folks at home telling their other halves how the game has gone.

We will give it to FIFA. It was amusing in a what-on-earth, who-is-this-for, why-why-why kind of way. Almost as if the Super Bowl was surreally spewing all over our World Cup final. If only England were involved. We could have trusted our fans to boo this tripe into oblivion at the very least.

Wayne Rooney said it best on the BBC. He described it as ‘crap’, explaining: ‘I thought the best part was when it finished.’ In that moment, Rooney became a man of the match contender. Not many players for Argentina or Spain had performed better by that point, after all.

The FIFA vanity project started long before this half-time show, of course. Those inside the MetLife Stadium could hardly hear the rather random pre-match speech from Tom Cruise because the Argentinian supporters in particular were singing over the American actor’s words. Perhaps it was in protest at him not having parachuted on to the pitch. Could have even borrowed Donald Trump’s Marine One helicopter that he flew in on. Therein lay the first of FIFA’s many mistakes.

This pre-match role for Cruise – along with others such as Robbie Williams in a sparkly blue tracksuit singing the cringey FIFA anthem ‘Desire’ alongside Nicole Scherzinger and Laura Pausini, and Bruce and Michael Buffer announcing the final, and the trophy being delivered in a bespoke Louis Vuitton case – meant that kick-off was delayed. Not to worry. Only the World Cup final.

The World Cup half-time show was quite frankly nauseating and a symbol of FIFA's vanity

Half-time lasted 27 minutes and 18 seconds, breaking the laws of the game - if only England fans had been there, as they would have booed it

Wayne Rooney described it as 'crap' on the BBC and he hit the nail on the head: this was tripe

Infantino, sitting next to Trump, was presumably too busy whispering sweet nothings and begging him to post their picture on Truth Social to notice the time anyhow. Half-time lasted 27 minutes and 18 seconds, too. That is despite the laws of the game telling us the maximum time should be 15 minutes. Again, not to worry. Only the World Cup final.

For the game itself, I watched this final on the BBC rather than ITV. Just my personal preference for Guy Mowbray and Alan Shearer as a commentary duo over Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon, whose input can be as cheerful as Bieber's.

FIFA issue those journalists attending a ‘VVIPs’ document. The one for this final was 11 pages long. It would be a good drinking game for those at home – take a sip every time the cameras pick out a celebrity. Oh look, there’s Will Ferrell. Oh hey, it’s Matt Damon. Oh nice, Adrien Brody, didn’t even know he liked ‘soccer’.

The only issue is you might be hammered by the first hydration break. But at least it would have helped you get through the nauseating half-time show.

Sports.title: World Cup fans slam 'pathetic' field for Spain vs Argentina final showdown after it was trampled by Madonna and Justin Bieber's halftime show
Sports.content:
Soccer fans were furious as the World Cup final threatened to be derailed by a wild and lengthy halftime show on Sunday as complaints grew over the quality of the field for Spain and Argentina to play on.

Madonna and a low-energy Justin Bieber headlined the show at the halftime interval as soccer's showpiece game was given the Super Bowl treatment at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

But the game itself had already been threatened with being overshadowed by the patchy field. On top of the blotchy appearance, there were multiple instances of the ball appearing to bobble instead of rolling smoothly along the ground.

Both Argentina, led by Lionel Messi, and Spain struggled to find any rhythm during an underwhelming first half that ended without a goal.

For many of the billions of fans tuning in around the world, the star-studded halftime show might have offered momentary relief.

But the soccer traditionalists around the world were unhappy at the near 30-minute delay in the game restarting, twice as long as the regular 15-minute break.

Dervoted soccer fans were bemused the halftime show for the World Cup final on Sunday

Madonna kickstarted the show alongside Brazil World Cup winners Ronaldinho and Ronaldo

The show was staged amid concerns over patchy parts of the field at MetLife Stadium

Madonna kickstarted the performance with her hit 'Music', walking out onto the field with 2002 World Cup winners and Brazilian legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho.

Bieber was then introduced by Ted Lasso for a short, slow acoustic performance while a montage of the tournament was playing on the big screens around the 80,000-seater stadium.

Shakira then injected some energy into the show before the performance came to an end and the preparation for the second half quickly restarted.

Manchester United and England hero Wayne Rooney had the most brutal verdict, saying: 'My favourite bit of the half time show was when it finished… I like all of them artists but I thought it was crap.'

The popular 'Football Tweet' account hit out on X, saying: 'Whistle to whistle, half- time in the World Cup Final lasted an absurd 27 minutes and 24 seconds. Nearly half an hour without football… all for a show nobody asked for. Just get the players back on the pitch.'

Other fans were worried that the field would deteriorate further after the show was over.

'I've been to public high schools in Texas that have a better football pitch than MetLife,' one observer wrote on social media from the game.

'It's an absolute joke how the final has been allowed to play here -- genuinely the worst stadium in the entire tournament.

Justin Bieber's cameo during the halftime spectacle was underwhelming and low energy

Fans were frustrated to see patchy areas of the field for a game watched by billions

Another fan posted a picture of the grass looking patchy in the center of the field, adding: 'Pitch is a disaster. Unworthy of a final.'

An alternative, but equally brutal verdict, from soccer page EiF Soccer said: 'The field quality looks so terrible. Slow, bobbly. Pathetic this is where the final was played.'

A different fan wrote: 'The quality of the pitch is disgraceful for a World Cup final.'

Former England international Ian Wright was in agreement, saying in his halftime analysis in Britain: 'The pitch is poor. It's ridiculous. It shouldn't be played on there.'

It was a cagey first half with Lionel Messi struggling to find patterns of play to get on the ball during the opening 45 minutes.

Spain had looked the more dangerous but that was without majorly threatening the Argentina goal.

Sports.title: World Cup fans reveal the VERY specific reason they can't enjoy blockbuster final showdown between Spain and Argentina
Sports.content:
Furious soccer fans have revealed the very specific reason they cannot fully enjoy Sunday's World Cup final showdown between powerhouses Spain and Argentina.

The wave of backlash centers entirely around the match's scheduling, with fans criticizing FIFA's decision to host the tournament finale during the middle of the day.

The final kicked off at 3:00pm local time at the open-air MetLife Stadium, forcing the world's biggest sports event to take place under bright afternoon sunshine.

Angry viewers quickly took to social media to express their frustration, arguing that the daytime slot completely drains the prestige surrounding the event.

Taking to X shortly after kick-off in New Jersey, one fan said: 'World Cup final should always be played at night time. Dark sky just makes the occasion feel special.'

'FIFA World Cup Final played in broad day light. Utter woke nonsense,' another wrote.

Furious fans have vented their frustration with the World Cup final being played in the day

Previous editions of the World Cup final, such as in 2022, have been held at night time

Meanwhile, one user added: 'World Cup final should be taking place at night. This is too much light'.

'World Cup final in the daylight and without any aura. What happened to the beautiful game I love?', another user wrote online.

'The game just looks like ordinary match... no aura and the sunshine is not fitting.'

The previous two World Cup finals - hosted in Lusail, Qatar in 2022 and Moscow, Russia in 2018 - both began at 6:00pm local time.

FIFA's Chief Tournament Officer in the US, Manolo Zubiria, previously explained that start times for the second half of the World Cup were calculated based on various factors - such as recovery for players and to ensure maximum coverage of the event.

'We've tried to basically strike the right balance,' he said.

With the World Cup final kick-off scheduled for 3:00 PM local time, it also hit a Sunday evening primetime TV slot across Europe.

The kick-off time wasn't the only factor of Sunday's final which drew the ire of fans.

Fans were left baffled as Tom Cruise delivered a pre-World Cup final 'Ted Talk' moments before kick-off, following a disastrous closing ceremony.

Fans rushed to social media shortly after kick-off to air their grievances with the timings

Argentina and Spain battled it out in the sweltering heat at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium

A bevy of Hollywood's finest had been billed as performers with Cruise headlining the event, designed to pay tribute to all of the competing 48 nations from the tournament.

However, fans anxious to see the Hollywood icon, 64, were made to wait for almost 90 minutes as they had to endure a bizarre performance from YouTuber IShowSpeed in the buildup to kickoff.

Cruise finally made his long-awaited appearance less than 10 minutes before the teams walked out onto the pitch. FIFA reserved the actor for the grand finale of the ceremony with Cruise reflecting on the tournament, which has been the biggest in World Cup history.

'So as we gather for one final chapter, let us celebrate a tournament that brought the world together,' he said. 'Let us celebrate each other. This is football. This is unity. This is greatness.'

Fans were left baffled by the address with one viewer writing on X: 'I'm disappointed Tom Cruise did not helicopter in for his Ted talk. FIFA missed an opportunity to collaborate with a chopper company.'

'About as inspiring as watching your cat get run over,' added another.

Others took issue with the message of unity with some pointing to the travel and visa chaos that some teams, including Iran, had to endure before and throughout the tournament due to US customs and border enforcement.

Tom Cruise opened World Cup final blockbuster with an emotional monologue

Popular streamer IShowSpeed kickstarted the World Cup final closing ceremony

'Brought the world together. You banned Iran from entering your country until game day,' one fan claimed on X. 'And banned a referee from turning up.'

'That had nothing to do with football,' insisted another. 'Just more USA’in (sic) c**p. How did the USA treat the Iranian team and players? Disgracefully, as fittingly represents the USA.'

The Mission Impossible star has been spotted in the stands throughout the tournament and performed a stunt at the Paris Olympics' closing ceremony

Cruise had been billed as the main attraction, but fans were left confused to first see IShowSpeed dominating their screens rather than the legendary actor when the closing ceremony got underway.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker’s son won thousands with stunning seven-fold World Cup final bet
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker’s son won thousands with stunning seven-fold World Cup final bet

George Lineker will be hoping to repeat the trick when Argentina and Spain clash in Sunday's World Cup final

View Image Gary Lineker's son George landed a monster bet at the World Cup 2022 in Qatar (Image: WireImage)

Gary Lineker was one of England’s greatest World Cup heroes during his playing days. The former Three Lions striker won the Golden Boot at Mexico in 1986 and finished his international career with 10 World Cup goals – a national record that stood for 40 years before Harry Kane finally overtook him earlier this summer.

‌



He is also a familiar face at the tournament as a broadcaster, firstly fronting the BBC’s live coverage for decades and now starring on Netflix with his hugely popular The Rest Is Football podcast. And one of his sons also has a memorable World Cup story to tell as well.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The 2022 final in Qatar is widely regarded as one of the greatest matches in football history, with Lionel Messi inspiring Argentina to victory over France after an extraordinary 3-3 draw that featured a Kylian Mbappe hat-trick before a dramatic penalty shootout. It also proved unforgettable for Gary’s eldest son, George, who landed a sizeable four-figure payout after placing an ambitious seven-fold accumulator on the match.

The 34-year-old entrepreneur staked just £20.03 at odds of 170/1, walking away with a tidy return of £4,276.40. George correctly predicted that both Messi and Mbappe would find the net, while also backing the score to be 2-2 after 90 minutes.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



He also successfully tipped Argentina to lift the trophy on penalties, with his remaining selections centred on the total number of corners and yellow cards shown during the match. Sharing the winning bet slip on social media, he joked: “If anyone deserves to win a bet, I think it’s me. Thank you all.”

Gary Lineker appears on BBC high earners list despite quitting over a year ago READ MORE :

“Haha…you were due one. Congrats mate,” replied Piers Morgan, while his son Spencer quipped: “The only good thing to come out of this.”

That triumph in Qatar finally completed Messi’s glittering career, with the Argentina captain finally lifting the one major trophy that had previously eluded him. Widely regarded as the greatest footballer of all time, the 39-year-old now has the chance to make even more history by becoming a back-to-back World Cup winner.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Argentina booked their place in Sunday’s final after a dramatic comeback victory over England on Wednesday evening, with Messi pulling the strings once again by providing two crucial assists. George Lineker will no doubt be hoping lightning strikes twice as he looks to land another money-spinning World Cup final punt.

Sports.title: Scottie Scheffler breaks silence on Bryson DeChambeau penalty controversy at The Open
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler breaks silence on Bryson DeChambeau penalty controversy at The Open

Bryson DeChambeau was handed a two-shot penalty during The Open after he was deemed to have improved his lie during his second round, with world number one Scottie Scheffler now weighing in on the matter

View 2 Images Scottie Scheffler has broken his silence on the Bryson DeChambeau controversy (Image: Sky Sports)

Controversial golf star Bryson DeChambeau is 'definitely not a cheater', according to world number one Scottie Scheffler, after the bolshy American received a two-shot penalty at The Open following an inadvertent breach when he improved his lie during his second round.

‌



Scheffler believes more players are pushing the lines on what is permitted on the course and he has suggested that the type of incidents which landed DeChambeau in hot water require stricter oversight, with the penalised superstar facing greater scrutiny than most. However, he believes that DeChambeau was sloppy rather than deliberately dishonest in his actions.

‌



The four-time major champion had previously stayed tight-lipped on the subject, stating: "I do have a ton to say. I haven't decided exactly what I want to say publicly yet."

‌



But now he's broken his silence on the controversy. "I think that opens up a greater discussion that - all I can really say is I think maybe we need to be a little bit more strict in the way that we are policing guys," Scheffler remarked.

"But it's a little bit of a balance because you've got certain guys like a Bryson who every shot he hits is going to be shown on TV. When you have camera angles that are far away, things can look different than they do when you're right there.

Scottie Scheffler rages at The Open as tempers flare in dramatic scenes READ MORE :

"We've done a good job of - I don't know, I hate saying stuff out here because I don't want anything to get taken out of context. All I'll say is Bryson, I've known him for a long time, and he's a lot of things, but he's definitely not a cheater.

‌



"I've never seen him cheat once, whether we were having a putting contest on the putting green or chipping contest, or anytime we played amateur golf, I never saw anything suspicious.

"When you're watching him there from that camera angle, maybe he was a touch careless around his ball, but I don't think he did anything intentionally.

View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau was angered by his penalty following the second round of The Open (Image: Getty)

‌



"We've seen penalties happen with - like you remember Jon Rahm a couple years ago at the Memorial when his ball moved in the rough, and it's like to the naked eye, can you really tell that?".

"I think sometimes it's just a difficult position in the game of golf. When I was growing up, if this was the line between things that were - like if this was the line, here are the rules and this was the right side of it and this is when you're doing things against the rule, you always tried to stray really far that way. I feel like at times, sometimes you see players maybe push it a little bit further than they should."

Two-time US Open champion DeChambeau became embroiled in a prolonged and heated exchange with R&A rules officials before the penalty was handed down. That post-round confrontation resulted in a delay to the release of Saturday's tee times.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rory McIlroy made clear he felt it was beside the point whether DeChambeau had cheated or not, expressing his frustration at the American's conduct. The Ryder Cup stalwart accused DeChambeau of holding the tournament to ransom and was scathing in his assessment.

"I think there's no doubt that he improved the line of his backswing," McIlroy said. "Whether it was careless or whether it was intentional, I don't think it matters. Hopefully it was careless, but I think the two-shot penalty was justified for sure.

Article continues below

"I won't pretend to defend Bryson," he continued. "I'm not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it's performative. I think a lot of it's for attention.

"To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn't feel like it was a great look."

Sports.title: Gary Lineker makes instant England prediction after France and responds to Bukayo Saka
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker makes instant England prediction after France and responds to Bukayo Saka

Gary Lineker has made an early prediction for England ahead of Euro 2028

View 2 Images Former England star Gary Lineker has had his say on the Three Lions' hopes for Euro 2028. (Image: The Rest Is Football.)

Gary Lineker believes England can go and win Euro 2028 after they demolished France in their third place match in Miami. England hammered Les Bleus 6-4 in a surprising end to the Three Lions' World Cup campaign, claiming the bronze medal and their best ever finish at a World Cup since winning the tournament in 1966.

‌



Speaking on The Rest Is Football podcast, Lineker said: "I told you this was the game we'd all been waiting for. England have put six past France and finished third at the World Cup, confirming their best ever performance since 1966.

‌



"It was a good way for England to finish the tournament. It felt a bit like a testamonial game, but all in all, it was actually very entertaining.

‌



World Cup final chaos as furious fans forced to wait HOURS to enter stadium READ MORE :

Arsenal eye shock transfer for England World Cup hero after Morgan Rogers snub READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"To be honest, after the levels of that performance , it's hard not to see us winning the Euros." Lineker burst into laughter after the remark and Micah Richards told his fellow presenter to 'stop it.'

One of the major talking points after the game was Bukayo Saka and his absence from the England starting XI in the semi-final defeat to Argentina, scoring a hat-trick in the demolition job on France.

‌



Speaking after the game, Saka made it clear that he wasn't injured and was fully fit, with Thomas Tuchel admitting he felt obliged to manage the Arsenal man's minutes having struggled with injuries.

"Of course, I would love to have played more," Saka told the BBC after the game. "But of course, it's not the time to talk about out that now. I try to do my talking on the pitch. It's done now. Move on."

When asked if he was fully fit, the Arsenal winger replied: "Yeah. I'm fit. I'm fit."

‌



View 2 Images Bukayo Saka spoke after netting a hat-trick (Image: FIFA)

Lineker asked his panel on the Rest is Football: "What about Saka? He got a hat-trick but he didn't play a minute in the semi-final. You thought, if he's protecting him then he won't play a minute in the third-place game.

"But he does and he scores an excellent hattrick. What do you think?"

‌



"I understand why Tuchel played Rogers in that game," Richards replied. "For the transition, but for him not to come on, talking about Saka and his fitness, his and Rice's fitness all tournament has been a question.

"But for him not to feature, is just bizarre and I can't get my head around why."

"You know when he's been on the pitch," Lineker interjected. "He's got a goal and an assist every 59 minutes that he's played. Three goals and three assists."

Article continues below

Richards replied: "The thing is about Saka, he gets you fouls as well and he gets you up the pitch. How many times have we seen him going up the pitch and he puts his arm out and buys a foul?"

Alan Shearer also weighed in, saying:: "We were always told he wasn't quite right, that he wasn't 100 per cent fit. If he wasn't fit then he wasn't going to start him.

"It was strange he never came on in the semi-final and then to start today. It was brilliant for him to score a hattrick."

Sports.title: Harry Kane reveals England dressing room's verdict on Thomas Tuchel amid fan frustration
Sports.content:
Harry Kane reveals England dressing room's verdict on Thomas Tuchel amid fan frustration

Thomas Tuchel's name was booed by England fans when it was announced over the PA system before his side ended their World Cup campaign with an entertaining 6-4 win against France to clinch third place

View 3 Images Harry Kane is firmly behind Thomas Tuchel (Image: ITV)

Harry Kane insists England’s players are fully behind Thomas Tuchel even after their World Cup heartbreak. Kane insists Tuchel’s “enthusiasm and tactical experience” can carry England forward even if the captain admitted they are still in the “grieving stage.”

‌



Three Lions striker Kane also said fans have a right to be “sad and angry” at the way they lost the semi-final to Argentina and it will take time to get over the disappointment. England did at least achieve their best World Cup finish on foreign soil as they beat France to get the bronze medal and Kane says it is hard to swallow because boss Tuchel allowed them all to dream.

‌



Kane said: “It’s our highest finish in 60 years. The enthusiasm he has, the emotion he brings, the tactical experience he has. It doesn’t mean you’re going to get it right every time.

‌



“We want to get it right on the biggest occasions and he expects that from himself as well. He’s a fantastic coach. He not only gave the players belief but he gave the country belief that it was our year.

Get the latest World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

Harry Kane's sad admission to England teammates spotted by lip reader after France win READ MORE :

“That is why it hurts even more than other years because everyone believed we were going all the way. Everyone has to process it. He has to process it himself.

‌



“We’re still in that grieving stage, the emotional stage, and we’ll be in that for the next few weeks. It won’t be until the next camp where you think about what the future holds and what the next target is. We’ll have conversations as captain and manager and with other team mates and staff, to see where we can be better.”

Kane admitted he can understand the fans’ frustrations and Tuchel’s name was even booed before kick-off in the third-place play-off game with France. Kane said: “It’s so hard. I think the fans are behind the team and are behind the manager.

Should the FA keep Thomas Tuchel in charge? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel's name was booed by England fans (Image: CHANDAN KHANNA/AFP via Getty Images)

“When something like this happens it’s very emotional – and rightly so. We’ve all been England fans when we wished we’d done this or that and it didn’t quite happen. That will die down naturally.

“Before we know it, we’ll be back with our clubs and the focus shifts to Champions League or the Nations League. Things do move quickly. Fans have a right to be emotional, sad and angry. We all are, we all feel it.

‌



“We have a chance to change it but it wasn’t to be this year. There is still a lot of positives to take from this, competing against the odds away from home and you finish third. Keep your chin up and go again.

“When you take the job of England manager, he knows that if it doesn’t go the way we want it then he’s going to take some stick. That is part and parcel of the job. I know there are a lot of questions after the other night. We have to process it as players. I’m sure the manager will.

View 3 Images Harry Kane and Thomas Tuchel have formed a good relationship (Image: Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

‌



“It’s his first major tournament. He’ll learn a lot from the players, the situations, the pressures, the travel. There are also a lot of things as players we can learn from the other night. For now it’s just trying to process everything.

“We had a lot of good things, a lot of tough situations we overcame. The group is incredible, the best England group I’ve been a part of in terms of togetherness. The boss was a big part of creating that as well.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
