World.title: Week in Review: Hostages to the Past
World.content:
Bosnia and Herzegovina’s historic qualification for the 2026 World Cup briefly united a deeply divided country. But beneath the celebrations, old disputes over identity and memory continue to shape political life.

In her opinion piece, Kristina Ljevak Bajramovic says that a proposed law in the Serb-led Republika Srpska entity, criminalising the display of the wartime Bosnian Army flag, is about far more than symbols. She argues that it reflects a broader struggle over who gets to define Bosnia and Herzegovina’s history, warning that attempts to police historical memory risk deepening already deep divisions.

World.title: In New Book, Massacre Survivor Gives Voice to Roma Loss During Bosnian War
World.content:
Ribic was shot and stabbed but survived by sheer chance.

Believing him dead, members of the Serbian paramilitary unit tossed him into a pit with the rest of his murdered family, a grave they had dug beforehand.

Ribic lay motionless, pretending to be dead until the paramilitaries left. Then, covered in blood, he climbed out of the pit and fled. He was eventually found by two Serbian soldiers. When Sima’s Chetniks demanded him back, the soldiers refused, almost certainly saving his life.

“Some Serbs tried to kill me, others saved me. How can I hate Serbs as a people? I cannot. I have always judged people by whether they are good or bad, never by their ethnicity, religion, or the colour of their skin,” said Ribic.

It is a tragic irony that the Ribic family had originally fled for time to Serbia to escape the first wave of ethnic cleansing in eastern Bosnia, carried out by Bosnian Serb forces and paramilitaries from Serbia in early 1992.

Ribic’s father, Ismet, later decided they should return to their home in Skocic, believing the Roma had not harmed anyone and so had nothing to do with the war engulfing Bosnia. They went back home on July 12, 1992, the day they died.

The Skocic massacre is the most notorious crime committed against the Roma during the Bosnian war, but far from the only one.

Atrocities were also committed against Roma civilians in the settlements of Sase and Perici and the towns of Foca and Bijeljina. In April 1992, members of the Roma community were killed in Srebrenica and Bratunac, and many Roma died in the Srebrenica genocide of July 1995, primarily because they were Muslims. It was only through later research, largely based on victims’ surnames, that many of those killed were identified as members of Roma.

The first comprehensive study documenting the suffering of the Roma in Bosnia was published only last year, focusing on the persecution of Roma in the Podrinje region – which Skocic is part of – between 1992 and 1995.

Their wartime ordeal, however, remains largely overlooked, the story of one of the most marginalised communities in Bosnia still waiting to be told and properly documented. Justice is painfully slow, far slower than for many others.

“Roma people needed to wait a long time for their turn to come to be researched and their stories documented. The same happened after World War Two,” said Ribic.

Such is Ribic’s own experience.

Failed justice

World.title: EU Pressure Mounts Over Albania’s Environment Laws, But MPs Block Repeal Efforts
World.content:
Albanian protesters were delighted on Tuesday when European Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos called on Prime Minister Edi Rama to repeal amendments to two laws that enable large-scale tourist resorts to be built in environmentally protected areas.

“This is one of the greatest victories of the ‘Flamingo Revolution’,” declared protester Ervin Goci, a professor in Tirana.

The protesters have been taking to the streets of the capital for over a month in anti-government rallies that were initially sparked by an elite resort project linked to Jared Kushner, Donald Trump’s son-in-law, in a protected wildlife area that is home to flamingos, seals and turtle nesting sites.

“Even before these protests began, we had agreed with Albania that the 2024 amendments to the Law on Protected Areas would be repealed this year, also a repeal of the Law on Strategic Investments,” Kos said.

World.title: Bomb in a Shoebox: Inside the Secret Work of a Russian ‘Dissident’ for the FSB
World.content:
The trail from the label led investigators to a supposed Russian dissident living in Poland as a student: named only as Igor R. under Polish privacy law, but who can be reported here as Igor Rogov.

Rogov was the one who had generated the shipping label, listing himself as both sender and recipient, at the request of a friend who told him the parcel held nothing more than gifts. That, at least, is what he told investigators. He denied knowing what the parcel actually held throughout the subsequent court case, but prosecutors argued the surrounding evidence – his contacts, his correspondence, his role in the shipment – showed otherwise.

By then, Rogov had already been living a second life for years.

That second life, according to the indictment shared with BIRN, started in the Russian city of Saransk after Rogov took part in a demonstration flying LGBT flags. Afterwards, a man he didn’t know approached him, gave his name, and told him he worked for the Federal Security Service (FSB) – the principal security agency of Russia and the main successor agency to the Soviet Union’s KGB. He had a proposal: he could help with the trouble Rogov was having at university, in exchange for cooperation. Rogov agreed, signed paperwork making it official, and was given a codename.

In public, Rogov was known as an activist, connected to Alexei Navalny’s Anti-Corruption Foundation and Mikhail Khodorkovsky’s Open Russia movement. Behind the scenes, he was instructed by the FSB to write up what he saw there. His handler sent the reports back with corrections, prosecutors say, until they read as though someone in them “posed a threat”. He was issued a phone and SIM cards for contact, and later an apartment next to FSB headquarters. The money came quarterly, in rubles.

After Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Rogov fled the country with his wife, Irina. The couple were granted visas to Poland because of their opposition activities and settled in Sosnowiec, a town in Poland’s Silesia region, where they enrolled in university on a government scholarship.

Between February and July 2022, he began compiling something more specific: details on Russian opposition activists living in Poland, some of them under international protection, along with information on the Poles helping them, including staff at the Polish Ministry of Foreign Affairs running a scholarship program for Russian students critical of the Kremlin.

At his dormitory where he was living in Sosnowiec, he put it all on an encrypted USB drive. Sometime that summer, before his wife Irina flew home to visit family, he handed it to her. She was to send it on through a parcel locker in Russia. Asked later what happened to the drive itself, she said she couldn’t remember.

But Irina did remember, and later told investigators that she had known about her husband’s arrangement with Russian intelligence. As the marriage began to fall apart, she also told her friends that he was cooperating with the FSB. Polish prosecutors, separately, argued that the data on the flash drive itself was sensitive enough that its transfer could have caused real damage – undermining Poland’s ability to protect Russian citizens under its protection, and exposing people and procedures that depended on staying unidentified.

On July 9, 2026, the District Court in Sosnowiec convicted them both. Rogov was sentenced to four years for the explosive shipment and six for espionage, combined into a single seven-year term. Irina received three years for aiding espionage; the court lifted her pre-trial detention.

Neither verdict is final, and Rogov’s defence lawyer, Marta Smolka, said he plans to appeal.

The trial itself was closed to the public on national security grounds, so Smolka couldn’t discuss what happened inside the courtroom. What she could say was that she had hoped, from the start, that it would be held in public.

“Open justice is a fundamental procedural safeguard, and being deprived of it places us at a disadvantage,” she tells BIRN. “This isn’t just about the rights of the defendant. It’s also about the role of the media as the fourth estate. The ability of journalists to independently gather information and assess a case for themselves is a value in its own right. As things stand, the media know only two facts: that an indictment was filed and that a verdict has been delivered. Nothing more.”

World.title: Madonna, Shakira, Bieber and The Muppets light up World Cup half-time show
World.content:
East Rutherford – Musical headliners Madonna, Shakira, Justin Bieber, BTS and Coldplay were joined by Brazilian soccer icons and \”Ted Lasso\” actors in a spectacular first-ever World Cup final halftime show on Sunday.

The star-packed, Super Bowl-style extravaganza — a first for soccer’s showpiece event — also featured a tribute to football icon Pele, and a rendition of \”Seven Nation Army\” led by Gustavo Dudamel and featuring musicians from the US, Venezuela and Iran.

\”Sesame Street\” and \”The Muppets\” characters joined Coldplay and a New York elementary school choir to close out a performance designed to raise money for the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which promotes access to sport for under-privileged children.

The 12-minute performance meant the total halftime break in the match between Spain and Argentina lasted 27 minutes.

– Largest since Live Aid? –

Organizers had billed the halftime show as \”the single largest gathering of artists united for a cause since Live Aid,\” and \”the most-watched 11 minutes of broadcast music performance in history\”.

FIFA chief Gianni Infantino predicted \”a couple of billion\” people would tune in.

The extended interruption to soccer’s most important game had drawn some criticism over the potential impact on players’ performance.

While highly unusual for soccer, the show was slightly shorter than most recent Super Bowl halftime performances, which have typically been around 13-14 minutes long.

The crowd erupted with a roar as the show began with Madonna being transported through tunnels beneath the MetLife Stadium on a dune buggy driven by Brazil soccer legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho.

Her performance of \”Music\” led to an orchestra featuring the New York Philharmonic, Venezuela’s Simon Bolivar Symphony Orchestra and Iranian violinist Bijan Mortazavi performing the White Stripes’ \”Seven Nation Army\” — a rock hit that has become a global US soccer stadium staple.

Footage of the Norway fans’ \”Viking row\” celebration from this tournament led into K-pop sensation BTS performing their smash hit \”Dynamite,\” rewritten with soccer-specific lyrics, before \”Ted Lasso\” star Jason Sudeikis and his \”Coach Beard\” sidekick Brendan Hunt made a surprise appearance.

They introduced Canadian pop megastar Bieber, who performed an emotional, World Cup-tailored version of \”Everything Hallelujah,\” before Shakira and Nigerian singer Burna Boy ramped the energy back up with this World Cup’s anthem, \”Dai Dai,\” accompanied by Ugandan dancers.

– ‘Driving force’ –

Ggiant screens showed footage of Brazil’s late soccer icon Pele from 1977, addressing the crowd at the old Giants Stadium on this same New Jersey site following his final professional game. Pele passed away in 2022, months after the last World Cup.

PS22 Chorus, a New York school choir that has gone viral globally with YouTube covers of popular hits, closed out the show, with Coldplay — whose singer Chris Martin curated the entire performance — and characters from \”The Muppets\” and \”Sesame Street.\”

The FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund was described by organizers as the \”driving force\” behind the halftime show.

It disburses cash to community groups that provide education and sport to under-priviliged children in countries from Ghana and South Africa to France and the United Kingdom.

The fund aims to raise $100 million. It had passed $60 million before the show, including a $1 donation from every World Cup ticket sold, plus contributions from corporations, nation states and private donors.

FIFA has already announced 58 groups that will receive grants, reaching 400,000 children worldwide.

Even before the game, a parade of stars took the microphone to whip up the crowd.

Post Malone headlined a closing ceremony, and Tom Cruise delivered a monologue about football unifying the world — but was largely drowned out in the stadium by singing fans.

Robbie Williams, Nicole Scherzinger and Jennifer Hudson were among further A-list performers.

World.title: US soldier killed in Iraq while dismantling Iranian attack drone
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com)—A US service member was killed and another injured in northern Iraq while disposing of explosive ordnance from a crashed Iranian one-way attack drone, the US military announced on Sunday.

The soldier was killed on July 18 during a controlled explosion of unexploded explosives from the drone, while the second service member had a minor injury and is being treated, according to US Central Command (CENTCOM).

The event occurs as Iraq strives to convince international investors that improved security and economic reforms are rebuilding trust after decades of strife, despite regional tensions spilling into Iraqi territory.

During a recent visit to Washington, Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government signed a series of agreements with US companies and financial institutions on energy, infrastructure, aviation, and banking as part of Baghdad’s larger effort to diversify its economy and attract foreign investment.

The latest incident highlights the security threats that continue to impede Iraq’s recovery, with strikes utilizing Iranian drones and Iran-backed armed groups disturbing peace, resulting in lives and injuries, and threatening to dissuade foreign investment.

Separately, CENTCOM said that two US service members died as a result of an Iranian strike in Jordan on July 17 and that military troops subsequently discovered unidentifiable remains suspected to be those of a third service member who had been reported missing.

An investigation to confirm the remains is continuing.

CENTCOM said that it was concealing the identity of the deceased and missing service men out of respect for their families until the notification procedure was completed.

Following years of conflict, Iraq has increasingly sought to position itself as a stable destination for international business.

However, recurring regional hostilities have repeatedly exposed the country’s vulnerability to broader tensions between Iran and the United States, complicating Baghdad’s efforts to restore normalcy and sustain its economic recovery.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi carries Trump message to Iran; Tehran declines Supreme Leader meeting
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Well-informed sources have disclosed to the Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Jarida, that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi is carrying a verbal message from U.S. President Donald Trump addressed to the Iranian leadership. This message, which al-Zaidi received during his recent official visit to Washington, comes as the U.S.–Iran confrontation edges closer to a broader war amid ongoing regional military escalation.

The sources from the Iranian Supreme National Security Council explained that the Iraqi Prime Minister’s stopover in the Qatari capital of Doha on Sunday was specifically aimed at coordinating the core substance of this message with the Qatari side. Baghdad is seeking to evaluate the possibility of transforming this verbal message into a tangible Iraqi initiative that works in tandem with current mediation tracks led by Qatar and Pakistan to de-escalate regional tensions.

Diplomatic Tracks and the Backstage of the Upcoming Tehran Visit

Timeline of the Visit: Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s state visit to Tehran is officially scheduled for next Thursday, though Baghdad has expressed full readiness to move the date forward if regional developments demand it.

Iraqi Request for a Supreme Leader Meeting: The Iraqi delegation expressed a strong desire to leverage the special bilateral relationship between the two neighbors to make al-Zaidi the first foreign official to meet with Iran’s new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei.

Iranian Refusal Based on Security Protocol: The Iranian source completely ruled out the possibility of such a meeting, confirming that the Iraqi delegation was officially notified of the decision. The refusal was attributed to strict Iranian security anxieties regarding the potential exposure of the new Supreme Leader’s secure location, given that he has remained completely out of public sight since the outbreak of the war on Iran last February. Tehran noted that the standard official protocols and security footprint required for hosting a foreign prime minister would pose an unacceptable security risk.

Alternative Intelligence Claims: In contrast to Tehran’s official justification, regional and Hebrew media outlets quoted an Israeli security source claiming that Mojtaba Khamenei is not actually inside Iranian territory. The intelligence source alleged that the strategic messages attributed to the Supreme Leader are entirely drafted by Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Commander Ahmed Vahidi.

On the domestic front in Tehran, former Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif is spearheading a political narrative that encourages the Iranian leadership to maintain its current stance and resist external pressures until the conclusion of the American elections. Zarif based his strategic view on recent communications he allegedly received from several U.S. Democratic politicians. According to his account, these American figures suggested that a potential electoral setback for Trump in November could push Congress to take decisive legislative action to halt the war.

Conversely, the governing domestic alliance uniting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf remains firmly committed to pursuing direct diplomatic understandings with Washington to end the crisis. The position of this moderate faction was recently reinforced following a directive issued by the Supreme Leader, which ordered an immediate halt to internal political public criticism of state officials.

This directive was translated into immediate action on the ground, as strict orders were handed down to hardline, ultra-conservative media outlets to completely cease their coordinated media campaigns against Pezeshkian and Qalibaf. The state warned that any violation of this freeze would result in severe regulatory and legal penalties, up to and including the permanent revocation of corporate media broadcasting licenses.

World.title: Iraq’s Integrity Commission arrests electricity official over 4.5B IQD cable theft
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Federal Integrity Commission announced on Sunday, July 19, 2026, the arrest of a senior official within the Baghdad Electricity Distribution Company for the embezzlement and illicit seizure of state-owned electrical infrastructure materials valued at nearly 4.5 billion Iraqi Dinars (IQD).

According to an official statement released by the commission, a specialized investigative and auditing task force was deployed directly to the Ministry of Electricity to audit regional inventory systems.

The investigation revealed that the head of the warehouses for the Rusafa distribution branch had illegally seized high-voltage electrical cables totaling 4,406,000,000 IQD in value. The commission noted that the primary suspect executed the embezzlement scheme in direct cooperation with two civilian vehicle owners who assisted in transporting the stolen state property out of the facility.

The arrest was carried out under a formal judicial warrant issued by the Judge of the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court, in accordance with the statutory provisions of Article 315 of the Iraqi Penal Code, which strictly penalizes the embezzlement of public funds by state employees.

A formal seizure record was legally documented, and the primary suspect was presented before the competent investigative judge, who subsequently ordered him to be remanded in custody pending further judicial proceedings.

Investigation Brief: Rusafa Grid Embezzlement Case

World.title: Influencer Andrew Tate and brother arrested in Miami
World.content:
Washington – Radical social media influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan were on Sunday in custody in the US, officials said, as Britain seeks their extradition to face new charges of rape, sex trafficking and assault.

Karena Thomas, assistant chief constable of the UK’s Bedfordshire Police, said the pair had been detained \”pending ongoing legal proceedings.\”

The US Marshals Service confirmed the arrests.

US news outlet TMZ posted video of law enforcement officers placing the self-professed misogynist and his younger sibling in handcuffs and escorting them into waiting vehicles in Miami on Saturday.

Asked by an onlooker if he had something to say, Tristan Tate did not respond, the footage posted on X showed.

UK prosecutors, who are now due to seek the brothers’ extradition, said the arrests came after they brought forward 38 further charges against the pair.

The Tate brothers now face 59 charges in total — 42 against Andrew and 17 against Tristan, British authorities said on Sunday.

\”We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offences including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child,\” Malcolm McHaffie, head of the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service’s (CPS) Special Crime Division, said in a statement.

\”The CPS has requested the extradition of the Tates from the US,\” he said, adding that the latest charges stem from receipt of new evidence from Bedfordshire Police that brings the total number of alleged victims in the Tates case to seven.

Earlier this year, police in Hertfordshire, north of London, said they were reopening a probe into rape and sexual assault allegations made by women against Andrew Tate between 2014 and 2015.

They also face separate rape and human trafficking allegations brought by different women and investigated by Bedfordshire Police, which covers their hometown of Luton, also north of London.

\”There is no place for male violence against women and girls, and we will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us,\” Bedfordshire Police’s Thomas added.

– ‘Face justice’ –

The Tate brothers are also accused of tax evasion and money laundering in the UK.

Their attorney, Joseph McBride, said in a press release that the brothers \”are innocent.\”

\”We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts this egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free,\” McBride said.

The Tates are dual British-US citizens who have been avid supporters of US President Donald Trump.

Lawyer Matt Jury, of McCue Jury & Partners who represent four alleged British victims of Andrew Tate, said Tate was \”now facing the real prospect of extradition to the UK after years of public campaigning by the four British women I represent.

\”They have spent years fighting for action to be taken, and I now urge the authorities to ensure this case proceeds as quickly as possible.

\”Andrew and Tristan Tate are accused of some of the most serious offences, including multiple counts of rape and human trafficking. It is time they face justice,\” he was quoted by the PA news agency as saying.

In March 2025, the US state of Florida launched a criminal investigation against them. The status of that investigation is unclear.

Andrew Tate is one of the most prominent proponents of the so-called \”manosphere\” network of communities, many of them online, that focus on traditional masculinity, anti-feminism, and self-improvement.

He promotes his divisive views, often incorporating alpha-male and aggressively misogynistic themes, to millions on social media including 10.8 million followers on X.

In Romania, where they have been based in recent years, the Tates face allegations of trafficking minors, sexual intercourse with a minor and money laundering.

World.title: Iraqi dinar declines against US dollar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar declined on Sunday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,520 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,526 Iraqi dinars on Sunday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,525 Iraqi dinars and 1,515 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate dropped, fluctuating between 1,523 and 1,522.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Calm Antonelli takes sixth win of the season with victory at Belgian GP
World.content:
Spa-Francorchamps – Italian teenager Kimi Antonelli ended a three-race winless streak on Sunday to extend his lead in the Formula One drivers’ championship with a solid fighting victory for Mercedes in the Belgian Grand Prix.

The 19-year-old Mercedes driver came home 1.9 seconds ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc with four-time champion Max Verstappen finishing third for Red Bull.

Antonelli’s teammate George Russell, who began the race in second place in the championship, just 25 points behind the Italian, crashed out of the race on the opening lap after tangling with Hamilton.

Hamilton was fourth for Ferrari after an incident-filled race in which he almost hit a mechanic during a pit-stop. The incident was referred to the stewards leaving the seven-time world champion with the possibility of a further penalty.

Isack Hadjar, who began at the back of the grid, did superbly to work his Red Bull up to sixth, just holding off reigning world champion Lando Norris, who started 13th, in the second McLaren.

Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi), Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) and Franco Colapinto (Alpine) rounded out the top 10.

It was Antonelli’s sixth win of the season and came from his sixth pole of the year, the first driver to win from pole in Belgium since 2021.

It lifts him to 204 points in the championship, 45 clear of Hamilton with Russell third on 154.

\”It feels very nice to be back on the top step,\” said Antonelli.

\”We just have to keep performing, keep bringing the results and then we will see what will happen at the end of the year.\”

The race started in cool conditions under a grey sky with rain in the air as Antonelli made a good start to lead up to La Source, but he had no answer when Verstappen deployed his power pack to pass him through Eau Rouge.

The Dutchman was then immediately vulnerable to a counter-attack and both the Italian and Leclerc drafted past him into Les Combes where behind them Hamilton clashed with Russell.

– ‘Racing incident’ –

The four-time champion continued in fifth, but Russell bounced off into retirement as a Safety Car (SC) was deployed.

Hamilton reported that he “had no front end” control as a result of a car ahead moving across him and the incident was investigated by the stewards who gave Hamilton a five-second penalty.

A downcast Russell, whose title bid had taken a heavy blow, said: “It was a racing incident, but it shouldn’t have happened if I’d had the speed down the straight.”

Racing resumed on lap five with Piastri fighting and resisting Hamilton before Verstappen swept past Leclerc for second. Piastri then chased Leclerc and they touched at Les Combes, where the Monegasque defended and the Australian lost a piece of front wing end plate.

The stewards investigated again, but took ‘no further action’ while Hamilton advanced and passed Piastri for fourth on lap nine as the race settled after a frantic start with Antonelli two seconds clear of Verstappen at the front ahead of both Ferraris.

Further Virtual Safety Cars (VSC) intervened and on lap 20, Ferrari went for a ‘double-stack’. Leclerc went through cleanly but Hamilton, who had to serve his five-second penalty, made a messy exit touching a mechanic on exit.

The mechanic was reported to be fine but the stewards decided to investigate again for an unsafe release.

That left Norris, who had started 13th with a 10-place grid penalty, for taking a new battery, leading ahead of Leclerc, Antonelli and Verstappen until the Ferrari cruised by to take command on lap 23.

Antonelli swept past Norris three laps later and surged after Leclerc while Hamilton, who had requested a wing adjustment in vain during his pit-stop, fell back to sixth.

Norris finally pitted to swap his old hards for mediums on lap 31, rejoining eighth after a slow stop due to a sticky left rear, Hadjar rising to sixth behind Hamilton.

Leclerc led until lap 34 when, as he feared, Antonelli’s superior power carried him through at Les Combes.

But he hung on tight, within a second of the silver arrow, while Hamilton passed Piastri for fourth with five laps to go

World.title: Iraq proposes Energy City project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announced the Energy City project on Thursday as part of a government plan to enhance energy infrastructure and strengthen partnerships with major international firms.

Al-Zaidi announced the Energy City initiative during an official visit to the United States, which included discussions with US officials and executives from American energy businesses.

This visit is part of Baghdad’s efforts to attract new investments that support plans to increase oil production, develop the gas sector, and enhance electricity generation capacity.

The Iraqi government is depending on the new project to turn the al-Faw Peninsula into an integrated center for the oil, gas, and electricity industries, taking advantage of its strategic location on the Arabian Gulf and proximity to oil export routes and the Development Road project.

The development takes place as Iraq continues to implement plans to eliminate gas flaring, expand domestic gas output, and reduce dependency on imported fuel for power plants, all while increasing refining capacity.

Al-Zaidi’s announcement took place during his participation in the Iraqi-American Chamber of Commerce’s Joint Economic Dialogue Forum in Houston, Texas, to finalize over $60 billion in deals with US energy companies.

The prime minister explained that the project includes integrated complexes for crude oil refining, gas production, processing units, and power plants, as well as connections to strategic oil pipelines and the Development Road, strengthening Iraq’s position as a regional energy and logistics hub.

Al-Zaidi highlighted that Iraq is seeking strategic partners, rather than just contractors, who can assist with technology transfer and contribute to the creation of new job opportunities.

Chairman of the Bilateral Chamber of Commerce David Phillips confirmed the Texas business community’s and large American firms’ willingness to invest in Iraq, notably in oil, gas, and energy projects.

World.title: DMK confirms TOI report it’s open to rethink on delimit bill
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Let govt bring the bill on raising the strength of Lok Sabha, then

will spell out its stand, the regional party with a crucial bloc of 22 MPs in the House said Sunday, confirming that the party is willing to revisit its stand on delimitation if its provisions do not harm the interest of southern states.

Senior DMK functionary Tiruchi Siva said govt should first make it clear as to what is on its mind as his party wants more clarity on the matter. TOI had exclusively reported Saturday that DMK is open to negotiation with govt if it is given an ironclad guarantee that the interests of southern states will not be adversely affected.

âI want to underscore if southern states are affected, then we will not accept it in any manner.

Our representation in Parliament should remain...,â he said in what appeared to be his pitch for maintaining the existing share of strength of southern states. As part of INDIA bloc in the last Parliament session, DMK was at the forefront of protest against the constitution amendment bill, which was eventually defeated as a joint opposition denied a two-thirds majority govt needed for its passage.

DMK is no longer part of INDIA bloc as its ally Congress joined hands with actor Vijay-led TVK, which trounced the M K Stalin-led party in the Tamil Nadu assembly polls, giving rise to the possibility that it may be open to business with BJP on renegotiated terms.





Asked about Shahâs assurance, Siva said, âHe (Shah) had said he will bring a bill. Let the bill come out and we will spell out DMKâs stand.â

To a question about his stand if the seats are raised by 50% in all states, he said he will not react to speculation.

World.title: Minister Manohar Lal dismantles Central Public Works Department’s ‘Delhi Club’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: For a long time, a group of officials belonging to

(CPWD) have attracted both envy and admiration for something they seem to possess in abundance â their tenacious rootedness while holding transferable jobs.

Housing and urban affairs minister Manohar Lal, however, revealed the secret of how they transformed into permanent fixtures, saying, âEver since we rolled out a transparent transfer policy, I have been approached by many, including some influential people, to get the transfers rescinded.â

Speaking at CPWDâs foundation day celebrations recently, the minister said, âI was told there were some people who never got transferred for 20-30 years.

No one was able to move them out. Big and influential people started approaching me for them when transfer orders were issued, saying they have known such employees for years. I told them that it would happen this time and we would see next year.â

Lal was referring to one of the most commonly known secrets of the city â the knack of CPWD employees in winning over Lutyensâ influentials who become dependent on them for their comforts, resulting in an equilibrium of convenience that few would like disrupted.





The minister said employees should think of what would benefit all their colleagues and not just themselves. He also urged CPWD staff to put in their best efforts to achieve public good.

Lal said as CM of Haryana, he had introduced a transfer policy for teachers in 2015 . He recalled that during former CM Chaudhary Bansi Lalâs tenure, when all ministers had offices on the fourth floor of the state secretariat, the education ministerâs room would be full during âtransfer seasonâ.

âI had suggested to the then CM and the education minister in 1996-97 that they should have a transfer policy. Some people paid heed to my suggestion, but said if it was done, people would be unhappy. They said no one would approach influential people with requests for transfers. Aur agar koi political aadmi ke dwar par koi aadmi nehin aayega toh usko roti kaise hazam hogi (If none will approach political leaders for transfers, how would they survive),â he said.

Lal said after the introduction of the transfer policy, people are happy as they donât depend on anyoneâs mercy. The transfers were done in accordance with criteria that had been laid down and a survey showed 93% of teachers were satisfied, the minister added.

World.title: Opposition protests invite to TMC rebels to all-party meeting
World.content: NEW DELHI: In solidarity with the Mamata Banerjee-headed Trinamool Congress, opposition parties on Sunday staged a rare walkout from the all-party meeting to protest the govtâs invite to its breakaway faction, even as both warring groups took potshots at one another, foretelling a fiery session of Parliament from Monday.Govt, however, defended its decision, asserting that it cannot deny space to the faction of 20 MPs who have approached Speaker Om Birla for recognising their merger with Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) and have already been allotted separate seats in Lok Sabha.âIt is govtâs duty to invite every group,â parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju told reporters. Playing down the walkout, he said it was only for a brief period as opposition parties rejoined the meeting soon.Facing disintegration and an existential crisis, TMC has leaned on other opposition parties, including Congress, which used to get short shrift from the party in Parliament when Mamata was West Bengalâs chief minister, to strengthen its cause.John Brittas of CPM, which has been a bitter critic of Mamata, said they supported the party in the walkout in the interests of parliamentary democracy which is under âattackâ from BJP.As Mahua Moitra, who is among the eight Lok Sabha MPs siding with Mamata, called the majority bloc of 20 MPs âtraitorsâ and demanded their disqualification, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, the chosen leader of breakaway faction, retorted that a âsmallâ party with only eight MPs no longer deserves front row seating in House.Mahua was joined by members of other opposition parties as she slammed the invitation to Sudip as the NCPI leader and to Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar as its chief whip and claimed that they cannot be recognised under anti-defection law. Only original party can merge with another party, she added.

World.title: Well-oiled labour supply chain facilitating illegal infiltration of Bangladeshis
World.content: NEW DELHI: A large majority of Bangladeshi illegal immigrants who sneak into India are not here to organically âexploreâ economic opportunities; they cross over as part of a well-oiled labour supply chain, with Indian employers in states far from the border relying on headhunting touts in Bangladesh for cheap labour.The âjobs for illegal immigrantsâ eco-system has touts at every stage â facilitating infiltration, transportation to job sites and arranging forged documentation before settling them into jobs across sectors such as textile manufacturing, construction and pharmaceuticals.âItâs an organised eco-system that comprises Bangladeshi recruitment touts who, based on requirements of Indian employers for cheap labour, identify unemployed Bangladeshis seeking low-paid, unskilled jobs in India. Every step, from their illegal entry into India to reaching their job locations, is planned well in advance,â a senior Assam govt official told TOI.The official said infiltration guides help the selected Bangladeshis cross over, mostly through Meghalaya, Tripura and West Bengal. Agents on the Indian side arrange their transit to Assam and onward train journeys from Guwahati to job locations across the country.Local touts help them secure forged documents like Aadhaar before another set of agents hand them over to Indian employers willing to hire them at wages lower than those payable to Indians.Assam, which recently busted one such tout network transporting illegal immigrants from Guwahati railway station to Tamil Nadu to work in a textile factory, leading to 34 arrests, raised the issue at the all-India conference of SPs of border districts chaired by home minister Amit Shah on July 9. The state sought a legal framework to hold Indian employers exploiting the Bangladeshi illegal immigration network accountable.Intelligence sources said Bangladeshi headhunters work on labour demand conveyed by agents linked to Indian employers. The network also arranges forged Aadhaar and PAN cards in destination states, enabling illegal immigrants to register as workers and move between work sites.âArmed with the same documents, many went on to project themselves as Indian citizens and even enrolled as voters. Special intensive revision (SIR), however, may have cut their dream run short by requiring proof of their parentsâ or relativesâ presence in the 2002 rolls,â a police officer told TOI.

World.title: Government may seek Parliamentary nod for additional spending
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With the fertiliser subsidy, other West Asia related spends and initiatives, such as the electronics manufacturing push through schemes for semiconductors and mobiles adding to the Centreâs expenditure, finance minister

may seek Parliamentary approval for additional spending, without losing sight of the overall fiscal situation.

The discussion around the need for Parliamentary sanction is in contrast to her ministryâs earlier stance as it wanted to wait for more data to come before assessing the situation. With the turmoil in West Asia still to settle, it is tough to have a clear picture, but officials indicated that the spending so far is higher and some of the expenditure, which will be matched through savings elsewhere, will need legislative clearance.

So far, GST and direct tax revenues have been on track and Sitharaman is pushing the department of investment and public asset management (DIPAM) hard to provide some cushion through additional realisation. Her meetings with the DIPAM brass have helped the Centre rake in Rs 20,272 crore â a little over one-fourth of the target with more than two-thirds of the fiscal year left.

A huge comfort will come if DIPAM manages to move ahead and finalise the IDBI Bank transaction, which has been in the pipeline for nearly five years.





With just two players in the fray, a lot will depend on how Emirates NDB, which has already acquired a majority stake in RBL Bank.

Prem Vatsaâs Fairfax, the other suitor, has a 40% stake in Catholic Syrian Bank and RBI will have a role to play in deciding its fate.

For the moment, it is the additional expenditure, which has prompted a rethink on the first supplementary demand for grants as the higher fertiliser subsidy bill needs to be settled.

While the fertiliser department had sought doubling of the allocation, prices have softened over the last few weeks, compared with the peak, proving some relief. The oil subsidy, which too has soared, will also need to be settled, although not immediately.

The Rs 1.9 lakh crore push for electronics manufacturing will require some additional allocation this year and with other ministries also drawing up replacement schemes for production linked incentive, some of which may have to wait, given the pressure on expenditure.

For a govt that has stuck to the fiscal deficit targets, despite facing one pressure or another almost every year, Sitharaman will seek to maintain her record and achieve the goal of 4.3% of GDP.

World.title: Even as fertility rates drop, young still aspire to partnership, parenthood, shows UN report
World.content: NEW DELHI: A first-of-its-kind survey of young adults (aged 18-39) across 73 countries, including India, by United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) shows that even as much of the worldâs marriage rates have declined and fertility has fallen to historically low levels, young people are not turning away from relationships or family life. Marriage, it says, remains âa common ideal relationshipâ arrangement among surveyed young adults.The report highlights that across countries â with very different demographic realities â many continue to aspire to partnership and parenthood, but say their decisions are increasingly shaped by financial security, stable employment, housing, gender equality and confidence in the future.UNFPAâs âLives, Choices and Futures â Demographic Futures Surveyâ 2026â gathered perspectives of more than 1,08,000 internet connected young adults, including 1,722 respondents in India.More than two thirds of respondents selected an ideal relationship and living arrangement that includes marriage â 36% before living together and 34% after a period of cohabitation. The survey says 16% reported remaining single as their preferred living arrangement.Its findings gain significance, as across much of the world partnership formation is occurring later, marriage rates have declined and fertility has fallen to historically low levels.âTwo thirds of the worldâs population now lives in a country or area where the total fertility rate is below 2.1 children per woman â the level commonly associated with the population size remaining stable over time,â the survey says.Among respondents aged 25â39, who ideally wish to marry or live with a partner, a quarter are currently single and not dating. The proportion is higher among male respondents (30% than among female respondents (19%).Financial security is the highest-rated consideration for partnership formation, cited as important by 81% of respondents. It turns out that economic and housing constraints constitute the most commonly reported category of barrier to partnership, rated important by 57%.The survey finds that among respondents â currently seeking a partner â personal networks, school or work environments, and online platforms are the most commonly reported channels for meeting potential partners, each reported by approximately one third of respondents. Overall the survey says more than 40% of respondents report spending over two hours a day on social media or the Internet for entertainment, making it the most time-intensive form of online activity examined.In India, while more than eight in 10 respondents (83%) said they feel positive or very positive about the future, nearly half of those surveyed (47%) said they are very worried about conflict, economic insecurity and inequality.While across most regional groupings of countries, two children is the most commonly reported ideal family size, the mean number of children reported by respondents aged 35â39 is lower than the mean ideal number of children reported by respondents aged 18â39.For instance, in the case of India, women aged 18-39 reported an ideal family size of 2.1 children, compared with an average of one child among women aged 35-39. Men reported an ideal family size of 2.2 children, compared with an average of 1.1 children among men aged 35-39.Parenthood is part of the future plans of most surveyed in India. Among respondents aged 35-39 in India who do not currently have children, nearly 85% said they would ideally like to become parents.

World.title: Less than half of 483 Lok Sabha MPs attended 90-100% of sittings in Parliament’s budget session, shows analysis
World.content: NEW DELHI: As parties gear-up for taking up a wide range of issues during Parliamentâs monsoon session â expected to be fiery in light of Ram temple and NEET-UG paper leak issues â the presence of MPs in both Houses is most crucial. An analysis of attendance record of the previous budget session, which ended in April, by NGO Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative shows that it is the smaller parties â with a handful of MPs â that have the highest average attendance record figures.Overall in Lok Sabha, as many as 101 MPs had signed the attendance register for all 31 sittings of the budget session â less than a quarter, or just about 21% of the 483 MPs whose attendance record was publicly available.In terms of average attendance record of parties in LS, RLP â that has one MP (Hanuman Beniwal from Nagaur â and RLD â that has two MPs (Chandan Chauhan from Bijnor and Rajkumar Sangwan from Baghpat â registered 100% attendance record for all 31 sittings. CPI(ML-L) stood second â with two of its MPs attending 30 out of the 31 sittings â as did Zoram Peopleâs Movement with its lone MPs. Samajwadi Party took third position â with 37 of its MPs averaging attendance of 28.43 days.Overall less than one half (45.7%) of the 483 LS members had attended between 90-100% of the sittings or at least signed the attendance register. The report examines the attendance record as available on the website of both Houses for the budget session to spot political party-wise trends and patterns.The single-largest party in LS, BJP (with details of 191 members available) averaged only 26.46 sittings per MP. Congress â single-largest party in opposition â averaged only 23.13 sittings (with details of 97 MPs available). Among regional political parties with more than 20 MPs during the budget session, TMC averaged only 15 sittings and DMK with 22 MPs even lesser with 14.64 sittings.In Rajya Sabha, 119 MPs â less than 46.6% of 255 MPs had attended between 90-100% of the sittings or at least signed the attendance register for those many days.The top 10 political parties clocking the highest percentage of attendance are regional parties. DMDK with its lone MP (LK Sudhish) is the only one who recorded 100% attendance, followed by J&K-NC with three MPs clocking an average of 94.62%. MPs from JDS, MNF, BJD, SP, NPP and SS all recorded an average of more than 90% attendance.Despite being the largest party in the House, BJP recorded an average attendance of only 84.39% followed by Congress recording 80.66%, the report stated.

World.title: 'Rise in instability in Iran': Indian embassy sounds alarm; urges people to leave, postpone travel
World.content:
'Rise in instability in Iran': Indian embassy sounds alarm; urges people to leave, postpone travel

NEW DELHI: The Indian Embassy in Iran on Sunday issued a revised travel advisory, urging Indian nationals to postpone all travel to the country.It also advised Indians already in Tehran to consider temporarily leaving the country using available commercial flights, as the security situation continues to deteriorate amid the escalating conflict in the Middle East.The advisory comes as military hostilities between the United States and Iran have intensified, with fresh strikes, retaliatory attacks and growing concerns over the security situation across the region.In its advisory, the embassy said, "The recent days have seen an increase in levels of instability and conflict in Iran."It advised Indian nationals planning to visit Iran 'for any purpose' to postpone their travel until the security environment improves.The embassy also urged Indians already in Iran to 'consider temporarily exiting Iran, using available flight options.'For those choosing to remain in the country, the mission advised exercising the highest level of caution, closely monitoring local developments and avoiding areas witnessing increased military activity, particularly along Iran's southern coast."Indian nationals who choose to remain in Iran should exercise the highest possible level of caution.They should carefully monitor the news to maintain full situational awareness, and should avoid locations seeing higher levels of military activity such as those along the southern coast of the country. Instructions issued by local authorities should be complied with carefully," the advisory read.The embassy also asked all Indian nationals in Iran who have not yet registered with the mission to do so immediately and regularly follow its official website and social media channels for further updates.The advisory was issued as the conflict between the United States and Iran escalated further on Sunday.According to Iranian authorities, the United States carried out fresh strikes on the under-construction Darkhovin nuclear power plant and other military targets, while the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it targeted Iranian coastal surveillance systems, air defence networks, maritime assets and missile and drone facilities.Iran, meanwhile, announced retaliatory drone attacks against two US military installations in Kuwait and claimed to have intercepted a US MQ-9 drone over Ahvaz. It also warned that the Strait of Hormuz remained under the control of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), amid heightened tensions over maritime security.The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said it was investigating reports of the attack on the Darkhovin nuclear facility and added that the site contained no nuclear material during its last inspection. The UN nuclear watchdog said the reported strike was not believed to pose any radiological risk but reiterated its call for military restraint around nuclear-related sites.The latest escalation has raised fresh international concern over the widening conflict in the Middle East as the war completes nearly five months.

World.title: Government issues a show-cause notice to Janakpuri private school, proposes takeover
World.content:
The Delhi government has issued a show-cause notice to a private school in Janakpuri proposing to take over the school, over lapses including “cover-up” of sexual assault on a nursery student, Education Minister Ashish Sood said on Sunday (July 19, 2026).

“In light of these continuous and systemic failures, the Directorate of Education has asked the school’s managing Trust to explain why the government should not execute the following actions: Government Takeover: Immediate takeover of the school’s management by the Delhi Government under Section 20(1) of the Delhi School Education Act (DSEA), 1973,” an official statement from the Minister’s office.

A three-year-old girl was raped allegedly by a 57-year-old caretaker on the school premises on April 30.

The Minister said that the government has absolute zero tolerance for any compromise on the safety and dignity of our children. “A school stands in loco parentis, it is legally and morally responsible for every child on its premises. If an institution covers up a heinous crime like child abuse, operates illegal branches in residential basements, and loots public funds, we will not sit quietly. We are prepared to completely take over the management and recommend the cancellation of their land lease,” Mr. Sood said.

The school management “deliberately” failed to report this heinous incident to the Directorate of Education, violating mandatory child protection laws, as per the statement.

“When the police visited the pre-primary branch to investigate the crime, all 64 CCTV cameras installed on the premises were found to be completely non-functional. The school had intentionally operated without a maintenance contract,” the statement said.

The school was “illegally” operating its nursery and KG classes from a private residential building in Narang Colony without any authorisation and the basement of this unauthorized building was being used as an unsupervised activity area for minor children, as per the Minister’s office.

“The school had no Child Protection Policy, no Child Protection Committee, and no POCSO-trained Nodal Officer. Essential security staff, including guards, had not undergone mandatory police background verification,” the statement said.

The management allegedly diverted approximately ₹6 crores meant for staff retirement benefits to another branch under the guise of “loan settlement”, and they also paid unauthorised professional fees to the school’s manager and trustees out of the school fund, as per the official statement.

World.title: Srinagar’s Vichar Nag temple sees puja again, L-G says ‘revival serves as a historic bridge’
World.content:
A ‘Pran Pratishtha’ ceremony was held at the historic Vichar Nag Temple in Srinagar on Sunday (July 20, 2026), once a hub of militancy.

Scores of Kashmiri Pandits attended the ceremony in an area that once hosted a number of Pandit families who had to leave their homeland due to militancy in the 1990s.

Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha visited the shrine and took stock of the renovation works.

“For millennia, this sacred temple has anchored India’s spiritual, intellectual, and philosophical journey. Its revival serves as a historic bridge, connecting our past, present, and future. It marks the return of a consciousness that, for centuries, nurtured an unbroken tradition of reflection, dialogue, and learning. Restoring Vichar Nag is a vital step toward preserving the rich, diverse cultural heritage of Jammu Kashmir,” Mr. Sinha said.

‘Vibrant hub of knowledge’

He said Vichar Nag holds a sacred place in the cultural and spiritual heritage of Jammu and Kashmir. “The revival of this historic site, once a vibrant hub of knowledge where scholars from across the globe gathered for intellectual discourse, is deeply gratifying,” Mr. Sinha said.

After a long hiatus, devotees gathered at the shrine to perform yajna and havan.

The Lieutenant-Governor was accompanied by Rajiv Pandey, Deputy Inspector General; Akshay Labroo, Deputy Commissioner, Srinagar; and Dr. G.V. Sundeep Chakravarthy, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Srinagar.

The Vishwa Kashmiri Samaj (VKS), a Pandit body, praised the restoration and development work at the temple complex.

World.title: Maharashtra govt allows hotels, restaurants, bars to remain open till 4 a.m. for FIFA World Cup final
World.content:
The Maharashtra government has permitted licensed hotels, restaurants and bars across the State to remain open till 4 a.m. on Monday to facilitate screening of the FIFA World Cup final between Argentina and Spain, according to an official order.

The Home Department issued the directive on Saturday (July 18) following a request from the National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI), Mumbai, which sought extension of operating hours for hospitality establishments on the night of the final.

The order, issued under Maharashtra Police Act, said the relaxation would be applicable only for the FIFA World Cup final and only to licensed hotels, restaurants and bars.

The government directed establishments to deploy adequate private security personnel to prevent traffic congestion and maintain law and order in and around their premises.

It warned that any untoward incident or violation of law would attract action against the establishment under the relevant legal provisions.

The order also asked establishments to comply with all licence conditions and directions issued by the Excise Department and local authorities. It clarified that the extended timings would not apply to any establishments other than licensed hotels, restaurants and bars.

District administrations and police have been directed to ensure strict implementation of the order, while all establishments have been instructed to cease operations immediately after 4 a.m..

World.title: CJP's night vigil begins, crowds camp at Jantar Mantar on eve of Parliament march call
World.content:
Banners, slogans and swelling crowds transformed Jantar Mantar into a packed protest camp on Sunday (July 19, 2026), as Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke's call for a night vigil drew a massive response ahead of its proposed "Chalo Sansad" march on Monday (July 20).

Amid the swelling crowds, Sonam Wangchuk's wife, Gitanjali J. Angmo, announced that the activist would end his hunger strike on Monday (July 20) if political leaders met him at Safdarjung Hospital and assured him that the issue of education accountability would be the focus of the Monsoon Session of Parliament.

Crowds continued to pour into the CJP's protest site at Jantar Mantar through the day as preparations gathered pace for Monday's march to Parliament.

CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das claimed that nearly 20,000 people were "at and around Jantar Mantar" even before the scheduled mobilisation.

In a post on X, Mr. Das said, "20,000 people are at and around Jantar Mantar. And it's not even July 20 yet. Dharmendra Pradhan -- your day of reckoning is in New Delhi." The protest also drew support from several political leaders and public figures.

Actors Shabana Azmi and Prakash Raj visited Jantar Mantar, joining Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra, CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat and AAP leaders Manish Sisodia, Saurabh Bharadwaj, Sanjay Singh and Gopal Rai in expressing solidarity with the agitation.

"July 20 will be a historic day. The Centre will have to bow down," Bharadwaj said. On whether AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal would join the protest, he said he had no information. Mr. Rai condemned Mr. Wangchuk's forcible removal from the protest site and urged supporters to keep Monday's march peaceful.

Addressing the gathering, Azmi reiterated her support for Mr. Wangchuk and the CJP, saying she had written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi urging him to initiate dialogue with the protesters. Prakash Raj raised slogans of "Jai Bhim" and said he would stay overnight at the protest site before joining Monday's march.

CJP members shared photographs and videos on social media showing the protest site packed with supporters, claiming people from different parts of the country had begun arriving for Monday's mobilisation.

Addressing supporters through a video message, Mr. Dipke urged them to remain at Jantar Mantar through the night, saying their presence was essential to ensure the Parliament march proceeded peacefully.

"Our protest is going on. Please come here in large numbers. Stay here for the night. If you don't come, they will try to end the protest," he said.

Appealing for restraint, Mr. Dipke said, "Our protest and march will be peaceful. I request everyone to follow the rules and follow the guidelines." He also asserted that Mr. Wangchuk's indefinite hunger strike was continuing at Safdarjung Hospital despite his removal from the protest site by police early Saturday.

"As you saw, they took away Sonam sir forcefully, but his hunger strike is continuing in the hospital," Mr. Dipke said.

In a significant announcement, Mr. Wangchuk's wife, Ms. Angmo, while addressing supporters at Jantar Mantar, said, "If political leaders meet Sonam in the hospital and assure him that they will raise the issue of education accountability during the Parliament session, he will end his hunger strike tomorrow," Ms. Angmo said.

She also conveyed Mr. Wangchuk's appeal to supporters ahead of the proposed march, urging them to maintain peace and discipline.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Wangchuk issued a message from Safdarjung Hospital through Ms. Angmo, describing Monday's mobilisation as "India's second freedom movement" and calling for "freedom from injustice" over alleged paper leaks and "freedom from fear" over what he termed his "illegal detention".

He appealed to people to make the Parliament march a success. The CJP also expressed apprehension over possible police action ahead of Monday's (July 20) march.

In posts on X, the outfit urged supporters to reach Jantar Mantar immediately, claimed tear-gas equipment had been brought to the area and alleged that anti-social elements could attempt to infiltrate the gathering to provoke disturbances.

The CJP appealed to protesters not to respond to any provocation and to ensure the march remained peaceful. At the nearby AISA protest site, hunger strikers Neha, Manish and Aameen continued their indefinite fast.

Neha alleged that police had attempted three to four times on Sunday to remove them, but students and supporters formed a human chain to prevent it.

"Today is the 22nd day of our hunger strike. Since morning, police personnel have come three to four times to pick us up. The students and young people present at Jantar Mantar have formed a human chain to protect us," she said, urging more people to join the protest.

Following Mr. Wangchuk's removal from the protest site early Saturday, Mr. Dipke began his own indefinite hunger strike.

Entering its second day on Sunday, the CJP founder said he had now understood the physical toll of a prolonged fast and appealed to people to strengthen the movement by joining Monday's Parliament march in large numbers.

The CJP has been protesting at Jantar Mantar since June 20, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, reforms in the examination system and justice for affected students.

The outfit has called for a "Chalo Sansad" march to Parliament on Monday (July 20), the opening day of the Monsoon Session.

World.title: Security up in Delhi ahead of Parliament session, CJP rally
World.content:
The Delhi Police on Sunday said the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) had not sought any permission for its proposed march to Parliament on July 20.

Owing to the enforcement of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (erstwhile Section 144 CrPC) that prohibits unlawful assembly of more than five persons, no protests, marches or demonstrations will be allowed in New Delhi district and Parliament Street subdivision, except at the designated Jantar Mantar protest site with prior permission.

Also read: Jantar Mantar protest updates on July 19, 2026

As per an order of the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Parliament Street Subdivision, the prohibitory orders were put in place on June 24 and will continue till August 22, 2026.

“In view of reports of a proposed march to Parliament by CJP on 20.07.2026 (Monday), Delhi Police hereby categorically clarifies that no permission has been sought or granted for any such protest march or procession,” said Sachin Sharma, Deputy Commissioner of Police (New Delhi).

Ahead of the said march and with the Monsoon Session of Parliament commencing on Monday, the officials said strict security arrangements had been put in place to “ensure public safety, security of protectees, and the protection of vital government installations”.

“Any person violating the prohibitory orders shall be liable for prosecution under Section 223 BNS and other applicable provisions of law,” the DCP said.

“The Parliament Street sub-division is a busy area with heavy vehicular and pedestrian traffic, and that police have received reports indicating that unrestricted public meetings, processions and demonstrations are likely to obstruct traffic, endanger human safety and disturb public tranquillity. Exercising powers under Section 70(1)(b) of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, read with Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Parliament Street, has prohibited the holding of public meetings, assemblies of five or more persons, processions, demonstrations, picketing, dharnas, slogan-shouting and public speeches without prior written permission,” an order from the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Parliament Street Subdivision, said.

The order also prohibited carrying of firearms, banners, placards, lathis, spears, swords, sticks, brickbats, and similar objects.

Multi-layered barricades

By Sunday evening, as thousands of protesters turned up to the site, members of the Rapid Action Force, Nagaland Armed Police and the Delhi Police were seen at the entry points, secured with multi-layered barricades.

Elaborate preventive arrangements have been made to ensure law and order during the Parliament session, the officials said. “Preventive deployment will remain in place throughout the Parliament session,” police officers added.

Security has been strengthened around Jantar Mantar, Parliament Street, Central Vista, Connaught Place, Shankar Chowk and other key locations, while rapid response teams have been positioned to respond to any contingency. Several police vans, buses and ambulances could be seen at the protest site. Protesters were frequently being asked to manage the crowd at the site, to keep the emergency gates clear. Announcements of Section 163 enforcement were also being made.

World.title: U.K.'s Burnham drops digital ID scheme to prioritise cost of living, say allies
World.content:
Britain’s next leader, Andy Burnham, will scrap government plans ​for a digital ID scheme when he takes office, signalling his intention ⁠to focus resources on kitchen-table issues such as the cost of living, his allies said.

Dubbed the ‘King of the North’ for his work as the mayor of Greater Manchester in northwestern England, Burnham will replace Keir Starmer ‌as Prime Minister on Monday (July 20, 2026), when he says he will also unveil his cabinet team of top Ministers.

Mr. Burnham’s office said one of his first moves would ‌be to ditch a plan for all employees to hold a digital identity document, a ‌scheme ⁠designed to tackle illegal migration but deemed a “fiasco” by a cross-party committee of ⁠lawmakers.

Mr. Starmer dropped the requirement for the ID to be mandatory in January after criticism.

Desire to refocus resources

“All the time and resources that were going to be spent on a national ID scheme will go instead to where it’s ​most needed, such as helping with the ‌cost of living,” Mr. Burnham’s spokesperson said in a statement.

Identity cards were abolished in the U.K. after World War Two, and Britons typically use documents such as passports and driving licences to prove their identity.

In November, Britain’s Office for Budget Responsibility estimated the cost of the ‌ID scheme at about £1.8 billion ($2.4 billion) between financial years 2026/27 and 2028/29.

“Labour have wasted ​millions of pounds on this project and now Andy Burnham is trying to pretend he’s riding to the rescue,” said Julia Lopez, a lawmaker from the ⁠opposition Conservative Party.

Lucy Powell, deputy leader of the Labour Party and a Mr. Burnham ally, said the savings from scrapping the scheme might not be large, but the move was “one small example of reprioritising”.

“This ‌is an opportunity to reset, to refresh, to look at those things that are perhaps not just taking resources but are taking attention away from government priorities,” she told the BBC’s Sunday (July 19) with Laura Kuenssberg programme.

In interviews with both the BBC and Sky News, Powell would not be drawn on other policies or details of Mr. Burnham’s cabinet team, but she said he would stick to the previous government’s commitment on new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea.

The ‌Labour Party’s 2024 manifesto pledged to issue no new licences but to honour existing ones, such the Rosebank ​and Jackdaw fields in Scotland, which regulators approved only for that to be overturned in 2025 after a legal challenge.

U.S. President Donald Trump was quick to ⁠seize on a possible change, taking to his Truth Social platform to say “the people of Aberdeen, in ⁠Scotland, are dancing in the streets” because Mr. Burnham “has stated that he will be opening up, all the way, the invaluable North Sea Oil”.

In another area where Mr. Burnham could ‌act, Powell also said the government has powers to put struggling water companies, such as Thames Water, into “special measures”. “Let’s see if the government does so,” she told Sky News.

World.title: 0 shots in 90 mins: Argentina’s unwanted record vs Spain in World Cup final
World.content:
Argentinian players argue with referee Slavko Vincic during the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Matt Rourke)

Argentina became the first side to fail to register a single shot in 90 minutes in a FIFA World Cup final when they were utterly dominated by Spain on Sunday. However, they still defended resolutely, taking the match to Extra Time.

Argentina’s task was made even tougher when Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the second-half stoppage time after getting his second yellow card, meaning Argentina was down to 10 players. Fernandez was carded for a reckless play that sent Spain defender Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air, and the card came out immediately.

Spain took 15 shots in regulation, Argentina none. Spain took nine corners, Argentina one. And somehow, 90-plus minutes of that sort of dominance wasn’t enough.

World.title: Shubman Gill on Rohit Sharma’s future: He has not told us anything
World.content:
India captain Shubman Gill has said there hasn’t been any discussion with Rohit Sharma about the Lord’s ODI being his last for international appearance. With an eye on the 2027 World Cup, as reported by The Indian Express, the selectors have informed the 39-year-old Rohit that the England series will be his last.

However, there hasn’t been any official word from Rohit or from the selectors so far. Having played two subdued knocks in the first two ODIs, on Sunday Rohit scored 138 in a losing cause. Despite scoring a century, it wasn’t the former India captain who turned up for the post-match media conference, where skipper Shubman Gill showed up.

World.title: Bloodshed in Balochistan: Why Pakistan’s resource-rich province remains in conflict
World.content:
For 10 days in Pakistan recently, family members of 27 policemen killed in Balochistan sat on a protest, refusing to bury their dead till the government accepted their demands. Last week, their sit-in ended after the authorities agreed to set up a judicial commission to investigate two recent attacks — in Ziarat on July 6, in which the policemen were killed, and in Hanna Urak a day before, in which five civilians were killed — allegedly by Baloch militants.

‘Operation Shaban’ was also launched in response to the killing of the policemen, in which 129 “terrorists” have been killed since July 5, Pakistani authorities claim.

This is the latest in a long history of bloodshed, militancy, and state repression in Balochistan, where Pakistan accuses India of fomenting trouble. Bordering Iran and Afghanistan, Balochistan is not just strategically important for Pakistan, but is also its richest state in terms of natural resources. Why, then, does conflict continue to simmer here? We explain, in five points.

Partition roots of Balochistan problem

When the British left the Indian subcontinent in 1947, the princely states were given the option of joining either India or the newly created Pakistan. The present-day Balochistan was then a collection of tribal principalities. Like many other parts of the world, the British empire had divided the Baloch areas arbitrarily, transferring some to the control of the Persian empire.

In 1947, the main tribal principality here was of Kalat. The Khan of Kalat, Mir Ahmad Yar Khan, wished to remain independent. However, as the months rolled on, pressure started increasing on him to join Pakistan, as the other tribal feudatories around Kalat all acceded. Isolated and facing Pakistani military pressure, the Khan finally acceded on March 27, 1948. The disagreement over Kalat’s accession became one of the foundational grievances for Baloch nationalists, although Pakistan considers the accession final and legal.



In almost every decade of Pakistan’s life, it has faced insurgency in Balochistan. The current one, which began under Pervez Musharraf, is believed to be the fifth, triggered by the 2005 rape of a Baloch doctor by an army officer at her home on the Sui gas plant, and then the killing in 2006 of powerful local leader Akbar Bugti.

Tussle over ethnic differences, natural resources

The Baloch are an ethnically distinct community. In fact, all of Pakistan’s provinces, from Sindh to Balochistan to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to Punjab, have distinct identities, and all three have complained, to varying degrees, of Punjabi domination.

Balochistan is rich in reserves of copper, gold, natural gas, etc. However, it is sparsely populated, and the Baloch people say they have not been allowed to reap the fruits of their state’s natural wealth.



Some of Pakistan’s show-piece foreign projects are in Balochsitan. China has built invested heavily in the strategic Gwadar port, the crown jewel of the China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC). The Saindak copper and gold mine is run by China. Last December, the Donald Trump administration announced it would invest $1.3 billion in the Reko Diq copper and gold mine.

Gwadar port on the Arabian Sea, close to the Strait of Hormuz, is in Balochistan. (Photo: Wikimedia Commons) Gwadar port on the Arabian Sea, close to the Strait of Hormuz, is in Balochistan. (Photo: Wikimedia Commons)

The Baloch people have opposed the exploitation of their land to fill foreign pockets, and pointed out that even the plum jobs of engineers and managers often go to Punjabis or Sindhis. China-funded projects, and Chinese workers, have been major targets of Baloch militants.



However, Pakistan government dismisses the claims of widespread discontent in Balochistan. Ali Chishti, a defence and security expert from Pakistan, told The Indian Express, “Millions of Baloch participate in the country’s political, economic, and military institutions. The insurgency represents a small militant movement, not the will of the Baloch people. Pakistan has consistently maintained that these militant groups receive support from India, an allegation India rejects. Attempts to portray Balochistan as evidence of a failed state ignore both the facts on the ground and the continued commitment of the Pakistani state to the province’s security, development, and prosperity.”

Baloch people’s demands

The Baloch insurgency in no way speaks in one voice. There is a section that wants an independent state of Balochistan and restores to violence for its aims. But there are many others who are happy to work within the constitutional framework in Pakistan, demanding greater autonomy and greater control over decisions that affect their region.



The discontent has evolved over the years. While there is a middle class that speaks the language of activism, petitions, and political representation, the violent organisations, such as the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), have gained in strength. They primarily target State or Army-linked places and people, but have also killed civilians.

Then there is the fact that in Pakistan, militants and terrorists are highly trained and have access to sophisticated weaponry, because of the NATO war against terror in Afghanistan. After the Americans withdrew from Afghanistan in 2021, they left behind large quantities of advanced weapons and battle-hardened fighters.

In the past couple of years, since the Taliban came back to power in Kabul, Pakistani security forces have claimed there are signs of collaboration between the BLA and the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), or the Pakistan Taliban.



The ‘disappeared’ people of Balochistan

A major, and very emotive, issue in Balochistan is that of disappearing people. Activists allege that over the years, some 5,000 people, picked up by security forces, have either never been found or found dead months or even years later. Last month, Maharang Baloch, a prominent activist working on the issue of disappearances, was sentenced to life imprisonment.

The state claims these ‘disappeared’ people have either joined the militancy or have left home on their own accord.

The State’s response

The Pakistan government’s response in Balochistan has usually been heavy handed, with Operation Shaban being the continuation of a long trend. Voices within Pakistan have pointed out that an insurgency that has local support cannot be rooted out through force alone.



When asked if the government was planning a political process parallel to Operation Shaban, Chishti said, “The State is always talking, but would not with foreign sponsored proxies or terrorists.”
